detail.abstract: Background: Nitrate in drinking water is suspected of increasing the risk of colorectal cancer (CRC). Drawing on the Danish national cohort study (Schullehner et al., 2018; n = 1.74 million) and the subsequent health-economic study (Jacobsen et al., 2024), this paper estimates the population attributable fraction (PAF) of nitrate-related CRC cases for Germany and assigns a monetary value to it. Methods: Two exposure categories are defined from the Wassertipps database (>10 mg/L: 32.5 million people; >25 mg/L: 3.0 million people; reference population: 71 million). The exposure-response function derived after error correction within the EU MARCHES project (RR = 1.06 per 10 mg/L) is applied continuously across the exposure distribution. Case numbers are based on 47,570 scaled CRC cases (ZfKD/RKI 2025, diagnosis year 2022). Direct treatment costs (mean €40,685 per case) are derived from phase-specific statutory health insurance claims data (Heisser et al., 2022). The health-economic valuation uses two VOLY scenarios: EU CAFE (€40,000) and Schlander et al. (2017, DKFZ; Germany-specific: €173,868, taken directly from empirical willingness-to-pay studies). Results: Assuming a causal relationship, the main scenario yields a PAF of 6.44%, corresponding to 3,063 nitrate-attributable CRC cases per year. Were the limit of 6 mg/L recommended by an international expert group to be met, approximately 1,821 of these cases would be avoidable annually; at 10 mg/L the figure would be 1,248 and at 25 mg/L only 147. Annual total damage is estimated at €908 million (EU CAFE) to €3,300 million (Schlander VOLY). The benefit-cost ratio is 1.8 to 17.6 for the benefit attainable at 6 mg/L (preventive fertiliser-ordinance costs, range €112-292 million per year) and 3.1 to 29.5 for the total attributable damage. Conclusions: The health-economic burden of nitrate-related colorectal cancer in Germany substantially exceeds the cost of remediation under both VOLY scenarios. At sites where the hydrogeology leaves little capacity for natural denitrification, such as well-aerated gravel aquifers, treatment at the water utility is a necessary complement to prevention. The repeal of the German nutrient-flow balance ordinance (Stoffstrombilanzverordnung) in 2025 is likely to increase this burden further over the medium term. One open question deserves mention: the rise in colorectal cancer among younger adults observed over roughly the past two decades coincides temporally with those birth cohorts exposed from early life to elevated nitrate levels resulting from the expansion of nitrogen fertilisation. Given the long latency of colorectal cancer, an investigation of this possible birthcohort effect would be of interest; given the strong confounding with lifestyle factors that changed over the same period, however, no association can be inferred from this coincidence.

detail.abstract: This paper looks at the effects of the non-aligned foreign policy towards the post-colonial countries from 1960 to 1985. By using a comparative case study analysis method, four non-aligned countries (India, Egypt, Ghana and Indonesia) are compared to two allies of the USA (South Korea and Taiwan). It uses the fact that one of them is a member of the UN General Assembly as an indicator of alignment. This paper looks at how the United States and Japan provided different kinds of foreign aid to the two groups of countries. In combination with Wittkopf (1973), Rai (1980) and U.S. Department of State documents, we find that there is a strong relationship between U.S. aid and political loyalty, especially in 1967-1973 and aid to non-aligned states is unpredictable and can be suspended, as in 1971 when India was suspended in aid. The countries that were aligned like South Korea and Taiwan were able to have steady flows of capital due to concessional credit and market access and so very fast growth rates. The policy of Japan that separated politics and economics was another source of capital for non-aligned states as Indonesia did after 1966. However, the paper shows that neutrality is not the only reason for slow growth in the first place. As we also see, domestic policies and institutions matter and aid voting linkage is correlational in nature and case selection makes the results difficult to generalize. Non-alignment was costly but it can be done and to a different extent depending on the reliance of the donor countries and economic management policies than neutrality alone. The paper provides some lessons for developing nations caught between the US and China rivalry.

detail.abstract: This case study examines JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s 2025 financial performance and considers how its diversified banking model, deposit franchise, customer relationships, and technology investments may influence earnings resilience. Using publicly reported company results and a limited competitor comparison, it distinguishes changes in reported earnings from recurring operating drivers and proposes two conceptual frameworks for understanding relationship banking. Revenue rose while reported net income declined in 2025; higher noninterest expenses and credit-loss provisions, together with a significant one-time gain in the 2024 comparison year, complicate interpretation. The paper argues that product integration and operating scale plausibly support relationship depth, but publicly available aggregate disclosures cannot isolate trust as a causal determinant of profitability. The findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating, not evidence of a causal mechanism.

detail.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) WLAN reuse is increasingly attractive for multi-gigabit directional connectivity in controlled deployments. In practice, adoption feasibility is often constrained less by PHY/MAC performance and more by licensing uncertainty and the willingness of key patent holders to provide implementer-friendly assurances. IEEE's Letters of Assurance (LoAs) offer an auditable record of such commitments and refusals, enabling early-stage screening of baseline and feature reuse choices before high-cost development. This article provides an implementer framework using LoA outcomes observed across IEEE 802.11ad and IEEE 802.11ay. We summarize the baseline implications of LoA divergence, translate these outcomes into a feature-level reuse map aligned to implementation clusters, and highlight a coding-layer hotspot that warrants early diligence even under a conservative baseline. We then propose a baseline-selection and enhancement-adoption workflow supported by a standardized internal decision record that teams can use to accelerate design sign-off and reduce late-stage surprises. The approach complements clause-level essentiality analysis and is intended as a repeatable screening method for standards reuse planning in mmWave deployments. This method supports early-stage engineering decisions and complements, rather than replaces, clause-level essentiality analysis.

detail.abstract: Methods for the early warning of cascading failures in large language model (LLM) agent systems currently report "early detection" in mutually incompatible units: the fraction of the execution log consumed before an alarm, the number of interaction rounds before a semantic violation on synthetic data, the number of turns after an attack has been injected, or the number of turns before a safety violation. These quantities measure different things and cannot be compared. As a consequence, the field cannot answer the two questions that matter to an operator: how much time remains to react, and how many false alarms will be raised on normal traffic. We propose PrefixBench, an open evaluation protocol and harness under which early-warning methods become comparable. A monitor observes only the prefix of a trajectory, and lead time is measured to one of four explicitly annotated endpoints: first error, propagation onset, explicit violation, and terminal failure. The protocol fixes six jointly reported metrics-coverage, lead time, premature alarm rate, benign false alarm rate with alarm burden, actionable margin, and intervention net benefit-and requires that methods be compared at a matched benign false-alarm budget rather than by a single AUROC value. We contribute the protocol definitions, a harness architecture that structurally prevents label and future-event leakage, a data and annotation design that combines fault injection, re-annotation of public trajectories and benign runs, and a pre-specified experimental plan with six experiments. Our central hypothesis is that, once the endpoint, the prefix-only regime and the operator-facing metrics are fixed, the ranking of existing methods will change, and part of the reported lead time will prove to be an artefact of annotation or post-hoc scoring. This paper is primarily a protocol and benchmark-design proposal. As a pilot, we run the harness on the test split of AFTraj-2K with two trivial baselines: at benign false-alarm budgets of up to 10%, they warn before the first error on at most 3.7% of failing trajectories, and reporting any alarm in the trace instead of the first alarm inflates coverage by a factor of two to four.

detail.abstract: This article examines the conceptual instability of compensation within international investment arbitration, where a growing reliance on financial valuation models,specifically Fair Market Value (FMV) and Discounted Cash Flow (DCF), has fostered a technocratic approach that risks obscuring the remedy's legal character. By treating compensation primarily as a financial outcome rather than a normative consequence of an internationally wrongful act, contemporary practice deviates from its foundation in public international law. Adopting a doctrinal approach, this study situates compensation within its proper juridical framework. It revisits foundational authorities, including the Factory at Chorzów judgment and the ILC Articles on State Responsibility, to clarify that compensation was originally conceived as a discrete legal response, analytically distinct from restitution and satisfaction. The article offers three primary contributions. First, it critiques the erosion of doctrinal clarity caused by conflating valuation methodologies with compensatory logic. Second, it provides a normative analysis contrasting the coherent articulation of compensation in general international law with its indeterminate application in investment arbitration. Third, utilizing Wesley Newcomb Hohfeld's analytical jurisprudence, it proposes a structured framework to distinguish compensation from related remedial concepts. Ultimately, the article advocates for a recalibration that preserves compensation's legal integrity while remaining responsive to the economic realities of modern disputes.

detail.abstract: Standard income inequality measures use perfect equality as a benchmark, but they do not distinguish inequalities that violate principles of justice from those that may be considered acceptable. We develop a norm-based framework combining Equality of Opportunity, Sufficientarianism, and Limitarianism. A norm distribution must equalize mean incomes across groups defined by circumstances, ensure that no income falls below a poverty line, and impose an upper income threshold. We characterize the implications of four principles governing income differences within these groups: Constant Absolute Reward, Constant Relative Reward, Proportional Reward, and Liberal Reward. Under the two constant reward principles, a unique norm distribution exists only when the richness line meets explicit conditions. Under Proportional and Liberal Reward, preserving observed income ratios or gaps may conflict with the two thresholds; we address this conflict by restricting the reward principles and defining an endogenous anti-poverty richness line. Using LIS data for six European countries covering 2010-2022, we measure unfair inequality as the divergence between observed and norm-based incomes.

detail.abstract: We study how reported changes in bank borrowing costs and collateral requirements relate to reported changes in fixed investment among euro-area enterprises, using the ECB/European Commission Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises (SAFE). The sample has 22,618 firm–survey-wave observations on 14,991 enterprises in 20 euro-area countries, covering survey rounds 2021H2–2026Q2. Questionnaire routing restricts it to enterprises that applied for a bank loan or credit line. Our primary specification is an unweighted categorical model. It includes country × survey-round × reporting-horizon fixed effects and firm characteristics, with firm-clustered standard errors. Conditional on the collateral response, a reported increase in bank interest rates is associated with a 3.4-percentage-point lower net balance of firms reporting higher rather than lower fixed investment (95% CI −5.6 to −1.3). Reported collateral tightening is associated with a 10.3-point lower balance (95% CI −12.9 to −7.7). Both associations operate mainly through a higher probability of reporting lower investment. An independently developed survey-weighted signed-score specification also finds negative rate and collateral associations (−0.03664 and −0.09824 index units per one-category step). Its coefficients measure a different contrast and are not averaged with ours. Neither framework detects collateral moderation of the rate association, but the confidence intervals cannot exclude economically meaningful moderation. The collateral association is negative in every robustness variant, including long-sample within-firm and lagged designs. The interest-rate association is more sensitive to weighting, reporting horizon and coding. The lagged rate-increase indicator is imprecise, whereas the lagged signed rate score remains negative over 2014–2026. Comparing respondents randomly assigned to three- or six-month questionnaires establishes neither different nor equivalent interest-rate slopes across reporting horizons. Computational verification independently reproduced all 38 archived complementary coefficient-table entries from raw microdata, with a maximum coefficient discrepancy below 2 × 10⁻¹⁵, and confirmed identical respondent-wave samples across implementations. Investment and bank terms are reported contemporaneously by applicants only. The results are conditional associations, not causal estimates of monetary-policy transmission or euro-denominated investment.

detail.abstract: We introduce the RIO Anchor Test, a designation-relative diagnostic heuristic that classifies system elements as constitutive or non-determinative once an Anchor-state has been explicitly fixed. The Anchor-state R is defined as the binary state consisting solely of one Constitutive Bond and its co-necessary functions. Classification is performed by clean substitution under a pure structural metric Φ that contains no impact term in its basis form: Φ(C) = 1 if and only if a substitute occupies R with zero structural additions. The method isolates non-determinative material (structural ballast) relative to the designated R. It claims neither unique objective discovery nor superiority across alternative designations. Secondary resource quantification is permitted only after pure classification. The primitives-Constitutive Bond, pure Φ-metric, and Rio's Principle of Clean Substitution-are formalized together with an operational protocol, principles of exhaustiveness and ballast isolation, boundary conditions, and falsification criteria. These elements support reproducible application, independent testing, and clear attribution of the methodological contribution.

detail.abstract: Enterprise software modernization increasingly combines cloud infrastructure, independently deployable services, automated delivery, observability, and data-informed operations. These capabilities can improve adaptability, but adopting them separately does not guarantee a coherent or manageable architecture. This paper synthesizes selected scholarly and standards-based literature on microservices, cloud-native systems, DevOps, and operational reliability. It uses a transparent, focused narrative-review approach rather than claiming a systematic review or reporting new experiments. The synthesis identifies five interdependent architectural concerns: service boundaries and modularity; automated delivery; observability and feedback; security and governance; and the controlled use of analytics and machine learning in operations. The literature indicates that microservices can support independent evolution while introducing distributed-system costs, including service coordination, data consistency, monitoring, and security complexity. The paper's contribution is an evidence-informed set of design propositions and an implementation sequence that organizations can evaluate in their own contexts. These propositions are not presented as empirically validated performance results. Future work should test them through comparative case studies and measurable operational indicators.

detail.abstract: Response to extreme heat and cold varies by age and health status. There is no age at which such exposures can be considered "safe". Households' adaptation to outdoor temperatures requires consumption of energy. But what if households cannot afford the cost of adaptation? This paper reviews the literature assessing effects on health of energy insecurity-inadequate access to enough residential energy for a healthy and safe life. Our hypothesis is that gaps in energy use for adaptation to heat or cold translate into health inequities at all developmental stages. Beyond individual risk factors, we advocate for the need to look at the structural determinants of health disparity, and the prevalence of interconnected drivers like race, ethnicity, nativity, income, housing characteristics, and physical surroundings that collectively or uniquely affect households. In the context of a warming world, we show that people who are the poorest and those who are minoritized are particularly likely to bear the burdens of conflicting mitigation and adaptation targets into the future. We therefore stress the importance of incorporating both indoor and outdoor environments into energy assistance frameworks and the broader climate justice dialogue.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework for understanding florimigration, a concept introduced here to describe well-being focused migration in which individuals prioritize post-material aspirations, including autonomy, self-actualization, and holistic flourishing, over economic security or survival. Drawing on Bourdieu’s conceptualizations of habitus and field, Inglehart’s theory of post-material value change, and Giddens’ reflexive project of the self, the framework conceptualizes florimigration as an embedded life decision shaped by the interplay between pre-reflexive dispositions, conscious biographical deliberation, and macro-level structural conditions. Migration is theorized as emerging from a fundamental tension between an individual’s reconfigured habitus and the doxa of the origin country, whose normative and institutional conditions remain incongruent with post-material value orientations. At the macro level, the realization of florimigration aspirations depends on the structural conductivity of both origin and destination countries, defined by the political, legal, and institutional conditions that enable or constrain international mobility.

detail.abstract: Sequential selection systems such as hiring pipelines, charging and plea sequences, admissions, licensing and benefit adjudication are routinely audited one stage at a time, and anti-discrimination law in most jurisdictions attaches liability to a particular practice, criterion or decision. This article asks whether every stage-level legality condition can be satisfied while the composite process still produces substantial cumulative exclusion, and what legal consequences follow if it can. It develops a compact model in which group-differential distortion at each stage of a K-stage pipeline compounds multiplicatively, with a dependence parameter describing how evaluative evidence propagates between stages. The model yields five propositions, each with stated falsification conditions. A stylized simulation, offered as an illustration and not as an empirical study, shows a pipeline in which every stage satisfies the four-fifths screen while the cumulative ratio falls to about 0.80 after four stages and about 0.74 after six. The simulation also shows that conditional stage ratios among survivors drift toward parity, which can mask upstream distortion, and that the effect of dependence is second-order and depends on its type. A comparative doctrinal analysis of the United States, the European Union and the European Court of Human Rights, the United Kingdom, Canada and Brazil indicates that each system selects an audit unit (a practice, an outcome, a provision or a procedure) and that, on the sources examined, none squarely addresses cumulative attribution across separable stages. The article proposes a modest interpretive heuristic, a stage-neutralization decomposition, for deciding when a pipeline should be analyzed as a single decision-making process. Limitations include the equal-latent-distribution assumption, the absence of original empirical data and the context-dependence of dependence effects. detail.abstract: On-chain transaction graphs in public distributed ledgers provide deterministic transparency into entity-level balance variations and coin dormancy. However, the empirical extraction of tradeable quantitative signals has historically suffered from look-ahead contamination, non-Gaussian distributional heavy tails, and metric conflation. In this paper, we propose the Whale Flow Composite Index (WFCI), an econometric multifactor framework designed to capture institutional and high-net-worth ("whale") capital reallocations in Bitcoin (P) without temporal leakage. WFCI synthesizes four distinct entity-adjusted on-chain dimensions: Cohort Accumulation Dynamics (F 1), Exchange Liquidity Netflow (F 2), Long-Term Holder Realized Profit Asymmetry (F 3), and Dormancy-Adjusted Capital Velocity (F 4). Each pillar undergoes domain-specific non-linear pretransformation to resolve power-law skewness, followed by rolling non-parametric robust standardization and sigmoidal synthesis under an orthogonal structural weighting scheme. Analyzing 5, 403 daily observations spanning from January 1, 2012, to October 16, 2026, we demonstrate that: (i) Augmented Dickey-Fuller tests verify strict weak stationarity (t =-7.0989, p = 4.22×10-10), confirming that WFCI is an integrated I(0) process; (ii) WFCI exhibits strict unidirectional Granger causality to next-day log price returns at lag 1 (F = 10.7721, p = 0.00104), whereas contemporaneous price feedback is statistically rejected (F = 0.8187, p = 0.3656); (iii) Non-parametric transfer entropy confirms robust net forward information flow (+0.00943 bits); (iv) Multi-horizon Spearman Rank Information Coefficients (IC) remain strictly positive across all horizons (1d: +0.0599, 7d: +0.1029, 14d: +0.0946, 30d: +0.0782, p < 10-8), expanding substantially to +0.2639 during the 2024-2026 Spot ETF institutional era; (v) Factor ablation confirms that removing any individual pillar degrades statistical causality or predictive IC; and (vi) A rule-based Mutually Exclusive and Collectively Exhaustive (MECE) regime classifier isolates the Bull Expansion phase (yielding a forward 30-day return of +18.41% with a 62.35% directional hit rate), while a Zero-Lag Exponential Moving Average (ZLEMA) trend-following overlay delivers a Sharpe ratio of 1.42 ∼ 1.45 with a 14.1 percentage point reduction in maximum drawdown versus benchmark buy-and-hold.

detail.abstract: Procedural terrain generation allows video-game developers to create large and detailed landscapes without modelling every hill, valley, or surface feature by hand. Fractal-based methods are especially useful because they can generate irregular patterns and detail across multiple scales from relatively simple mathematical rules. This review examines how fractals are used in modern video-game terrain generation, focusing on fractal Brownian motion, noisebased techniques such as Perlin noise, and recursive methods such as the Diamond-Square algorithm. It first explains why these approaches are useful, including their ability to reduce manual work, generate large areas efficiently, and produce natural-looking variation. The paper also examines their main limitations, particularly reduced designer control, visual artifacts, computational trade-offs, and the difficulty of guaranteeing that automatically generated terrain is suitable for gameplay. Finally, the review considers hybrid approaches that combine fractal generation with erosion models, Digital Elevation Models, and designer-specified constraints. The literature suggests that fractals are most effective not as a complete replacement for terrain design, but as a flexible mathematical foundation that can be refined by physical simulation and human control.

detail.abstract: From 28 February 2026, commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz nearly stopped. This paper measures what happened to goods bound for the Gulf over the next six months, using trade statistics, ship tracking, port and customs records and 125 graded claims from news and official sources. Container cargo reaching UAE ports fell to between a tenth and a quarter of its 2025 level, while EU container goods declared for the UAE recovered to 0.81-0.84 of normal by June and July. A capacity-and-queue model, planned before it was built and not yet tested, puts the EU cargo still waiting at the end of August at 0.6-2.0 months of normal supply. Across about 1,600 product-destination pairs, goods with more value per kilogram lost less, as the Alchian-Allen effect predicts, including products the UAE does not make. The sorting was modest: value groups explain 2.4% of the variation in monthly product shipments, against 14.9% for a shock shared by all goods at a destination. In a test fixed in advance, the cargo types that carriers restricted did not lose more than other goods. The value pattern appears only in the five destinations served by the Gulf liner network, a grouping chosen after seeing the data, so the paper fixes a replication on September-October 2026 data, a test of ship tracking and seven predictions for the reopening. A Beer Game model with the standard behavioural ordering rule failed all three of its validation tests.

detail.abstract: Agentic AI could create substantial value for consumers by improving search, matching and bargaining. However, obtaining these benefits requires consumers to delegate real authority over economic decisions to AI agents. This delegation could result in commercial providers of AI agents occupying a significant position between consumers and suppliers. Whether such a position develops into enduring market power for the providers of AI agents will depend on the competitive dynamics of the market for agents. Where market power does arise, the resulting concerns are likely to be familiar but proving them may be harder. This is because users and regulators may observe an agent's final choice without seeing the alternatives considered or the commercial influences that shaped it. Addressing this proof problem is likely to require collaboration between economic and technical experts to establish identify credible counterfactuals for how agents would have behaved but-for the alleged conduct.

detail.abstract: Preference-based Bayesian optimization (PBO) enables sequential optimization when candidate solutions can be compared but cannot be assigned reliable scalar values. Most PBO methods, however, assume stable decision-maker preferences. We introduce DA-MNL-PBO, a drift-aware framework in which interpretable multinomial-logit/Bradley-Terry preference coefficients evolve through a two-regime state-space model. A sequential Laplace approximation within an interacting multiple-model filter maintains stable and adaptive preference states, while a regime-aware acquisition rule combines optimization value with information about the preference coefficients and latent adaptation regime. We evaluate DA-MNL-PBO in a semi-synthetic predictive-maintenance study using NASA N-CMAPSS run-to-failure trajectories. Real engine trajectories and remaining-useful-life information define maintenance-policy outcomes, while controlled time-varying stakeholder utilities generate pairwise preferences. Hyperparameters were frozen before confirmatory evaluation. Across two confirmatory subsets, four temporal conditions, three responseconsistency levels, 200 paired replicates, and four methods, the study comprised 19,200 method-level runs. Under preference drift, DA-MNL-PBO achieved lower mean cumulative dynamic regret than static and sliding-window MNL-PBO in all 12 confirmatory drift conditions, reducing regret relative to static MNL-PBO by 6.9-71.1% (42.1% on average). Fixed exponential discounting performed better under all abrupt shifts, whereas DA-MNL-PBO performed better in five of six gradual-drift conditions. The method also produced meaningful shifts in maintenance recommendations after preference changes. These results support probabilistic drift-aware preference modeling particularly under gradual change, while demonstrating that fixed forgetting remains competitive under abrupt shifts. Because preferences are simulated, the results establish algorithmic adaptation rather than humanpreference validity.

detail.abstract: The legalization of marijuana has become an increasingly controversial topic across the United States. There are constant debates about its economic and social impacts. This paper examines the determinants of support for recreational marijuana among college students. Using original survey data collected from almost 200 random students and Christopher Newport University. This study analyzes how political ideology, personal experience, and demographics influence an individual's attitude towards the legalization of marijuana. Employing logit regression models, the results indicate that political ideology is the strongest predictor of support for legalization. Other factors such as demographics and social factors also play an impactful role. The findings suggest that ideological beliefs and personal exposure are important drivers for policy preferences. This study contributes to the literature by focusing on the college student population and provides insight into how younger individuals form opinions on marijuana policies.

detail.abstract: Which oil-price component is most closely connected to financial stress? Aggregate connectedness does not distinguish oil-related links from connections among stress categories. We combine daily demand, supply, and risk-premium shocks with the five sub-indices of the Office of Financial Research (OFR) Financial Stress Index in a time-varying parameter vector autoregression (TVP-VAR) connectedness model for 2000-2025 and decompose total connectedness into oil-related and within-stress contributions. Corrected total connectedness rises from 48.10 before the global financial crisis (GFC) to 59.64 in the GFC-to-COVID regime; within-stress links account for 9.07 percentage points of this increase, compared with 2.47 points for oil-related links. The risk-premium component has positive average net directional connectedness in the full eight-variable system in every regime, whereas demand and supply have negative averages. Distinguishing oil shocks and stress channels therefore reveals both the risk component's transmitting role and the contribution of within-financial links to the crisis-period increase.

detail.abstract: As companies struggle to conduct human rights due diligence and governments attempt to monitor compliance with supply chain regulations, they are increasingly turning to digital technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI). While AI-based tools can improve supply chain visibility and assess human rights risks, they carry potential risks of marginalizing rightsholders and undermining traditional conceptions of corporate accountability. This article examines the methodologies behind these tools, the role of technology firms in their design and application and the unintended consequences of relying on those firms to interpret the legal norm of human rights due diligence. It draws on a critical analysis of AI-based tools as well as interviews with officials from technology firms, consultants and human rights advocates. I argue that although AI can enhance human rights due diligence, AI-driven corporate accountability delegates interpretive judgment to technology firms, privatizes human rights and deemphasizes stakeholder engagement.

detail.abstract: When an exchange-traded fund whose portfolio is made of listed options is redeemed in kind, the option positions have to move at the clearing house from the fund's account to the redeeming dealer's account, and in 2026 that step still runs outside the clearing house's own process. In its rule filing of January 2026, NSCC describes it as "fragmented and heavily dependent on manual intervention, which increases the potential for errors." This report builds a runnable evaluation of that step and measures eight frontier models on it. The task is a settlement tie-out: given the redemption order, three portfolio composition files of which one is the basket of record, the fund's final net asset value, the clearing house's record of four position moves, the custodian's positions the next morning and the agent's own status report, tie every option leg to the basket, recompute the cash component, and decide whether to settle. The gold case has one leg moved at 12,000 contracts against 120 due, the order's underlying-share equivalent keyed as the contract count, while the agent's report says all four legs moved; the right answer is to hold and have 11,880 contracts returned first. A clean twin settles. Before any model ran, six independent attackers tried to make the grader score a wrong answer well or a right answer badly, about 1,500 graded mutations; every gate was then moved onto an evidence hook so that nothing fires on a missing field or a notation, and 267 of the attackers' checks were pinned as standing regressions. Every mechanical assertion of the fixture was checked against public primary documents and labelled. Then eight models from three vendors ran both cases once. Every model held the broken order and settled the clean one; nine of sixteen runs met every criterion; three models were perfect on both cases. The losses were arithmetic one layer down: a small model valued the option legs per share instead of per contract and fired the gate built for that confusion on both cases; a mid-tier model sized the excess at ten times its value; another moved the written legs' positions the wrong way; a small model converted a per-share impact to a percentage fifty times too small. No model assumed what the dealer had paid for its shares, though one stated its reason for refusing in the answer schema's own words. Running real models also found six places where the grader rejected legitimate answers; all runs were re-graded with the original scores kept, and eleven scores moved without any decision or gate changing. These are recorded results from one break pattern, one run per model per case, not rates.

This Guide presents good commercial practice for how attorneys should advise real estate stakeholders (professionals, investors, lenders, owners and occupants, insurance companies) on climate change and sustainability risks and opportunities in design, financing, construction, and sale or lease of new buildings as well as retrofits to existing buildings.

Chapter 1 explains that real estate development is an especially important practice area for sustainability and climate change. All human-made spaces, structures and surroundings that provide the setting for daily human activity are physical assets. As such, they are highly dependent on infrastructure and are uniquely vulnerable to the impacts of a changing climate, ranging from structural damage to operational disruptions to significant risks to the health and wellness of occupants. Given the significant contributions of buildings to climate emissions (approximately 40% globally), buildings are also increasingly regulated, from energy performance to sustainable materials.

Chapter 1 also explains the two American Bar Association House of Delegates resolutions encouraging lawyers to incorporate the risks and opportunities of climate change and sustainability into their law practice. This Guide is an outgrowth of these resolutions. It is intended to help lawyers practicing real estate work respond competently to the risks and opportunities of climate change and sustainability.

detail.abstract: In an era marked by prolonged and overlapping crises, organizational threats increasingly unfold as creeping crises that unfold slowly, lack clear beginnings, and evade timely recognition. Unlike for acute, time-bounded crises, traditional crisis management models, largely designed for fast-burning, high-urgency events, struggle to recognize and respond to such slowly escalating threats. This paper investigates how a creeping crisis can deepen and ultimately turn into an existential threat through the fragmented construction of urgency across organizational levels. Drawing on a three-year ethnographic study of a large, decentralized non-profit health and social care organization in Germany, we analyze how leaders and employees experience and manage prolonged extreme contexts shaped by resource scarcity, post-COVID turbulence, and systemic pressures within the healthcare system. Our findings reveal a two-phase process model: different normalization process and fragmentation of urgency. In the first phase, prolonged exposure to crisis leads to the normalization of extreme contexts, reshaping urgency thresholds through flatlining, disengagement despite recognition, and adapted urgency scales. In the second phase, we identify four recurring patterns that reinforce this fragmentation: strategic detachment at the board level, responsibility displacement at central institutions, absorptive burden for a team lead, and resigned normalization at the team level. Together, these patterns form a reinforcing loop that undermines coordinated action and delays escalation, allowing a manageable creeping crisis to intensify into an existential organizational threat. This paper contributes to crisis management and organization studies by theorizing urgency as a socially constructed, temporally dynamic, and structurally fragmented accomplishment in decentralized organizations facing prolonged crises.

detail.abstract: We develop measures of local temperature disturbances from hourly weather paths and study their relationship with subsequent economic activity. The measures preserve the timing and duration of exposure within each month. Heat persistence and nighttime exposure jointly contain information about later unemployment and nighttime activity beyond conventional weather measures. In a full-sample periodic spatial model that orders temperature before economic activity, the temperature block accounts for about 30 percent of unemployment forecast-error variance at one year and 41 percent at two years, compared with less than 2 percent at impact. In county local projections, the estimated association between disturbance size and unemployment changes sign across seasons. The squared magnitude of innovations outside the leading physical-temperature factor is positively associated with unemployment relative to total population six months later. This relationship persists when 2020-2021 are excluded and in data ending before 2020, while signed exposure responses are less stable. A single signed temperature index therefore leaves out variation associated with subsequent labor-market adjustment.

detail.abstract: Reported lead-lag relations between cryptocurrencies are usually documented for a few preselected pairs, without accounting for how many pairs could have been examined. We screen all 136 unordered pairs among 17 hourly cryptocurrency series using stochastic-crossover events, a binomial test and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. One pair survives: BTCJPY precedes SOLUSD in 57 of 81 directional matches (70.4%; bootstrap 95% interval 60.5%-80.3%; permutation p = 0.002). The result is fragile. It holds at windows of ±1 and ±2 hourly bars but not at ±3 or ±5, only 33.9% of BTCJPY events are matched, the out-of-sample block contains 16 events, and a second correction over eight validation tests retains three. The finding is methodologically contingent: uncorrected testing would flag about seven of 136 pairs by chance alone, whereas correction leaves one. Robust hourly lead-lag in this universe is rare, and an ordering confined to one or two bars calls for checks on timestamps and quote conventions before an economic interpretation.

detail.abstract: Global fintech revenue reached an estimated $504 billion in 2025, up 22% in a year and growing about four times faster than traditional banks (BCG & FT Partners, 2026). That headline hides a sharp divergence. A small group of companies that own payment rails, sell indispensable software to merchants, or hold the regulated balance sheets that customers trust are compounding at high margins. Meanwhile, several former leaders have stalled, been put up for sale, or seen their earnings swing with crypto prices and interest rates. This paper sizes the fintech market, explains what is driving its growth, analyzes sixteen of the most important companies in the sector using results through mid-2026, and maps the emerging trends most likely to reshape it by 2030: stablecoins, AI agents that shop and pay on a customer's behalf, real-time payment rails, and an unsettled U.S. regulatory regime. Each company is scored on five dimensions of business quality and then compared against its current valuation. The central finding is that durable advantage in fintech now comes from three sources, summarized in the title: rails (networks that sit in the middle of every transaction), software (platforms merchants cannot easily rip out), and trust (licensed, profitable institutions that customers make their primary financial home). Mastercard, Visa and Stripe score highest on business quality. Nu Holdings, Adyen and Revolut form a strong second tier. Nu offers the most attractive combination of quality and price among listed companies, while PayPal, Block, Fiserv and the crypto-linked names face structural questions that low valuations alone do not answer.

detail.abstract: Peru suspended its fuel excise on gasohol below 95 octane from April to June 2022, and wholesale plants and stations must register every price with the regulator. Comparing gasohol 90 with gasohol 95, whose excise did not change, at the same station, we follow the cut from the statute to the posted wholesale list to the pump. Each plant of the state refiner that registered the change lowered its list by the full tax on that day. Pump prices followed over weeks: they passed 0.84 of the tax after two weeks and 0.94 after five, net of ordinary list movements; when the adjustment ended cannot be identified. Almost every station cut within two weeks, at first by less than the tax. detail.abstract: The most valuable data about an investment are held by financial institutions, but that data is dispersed across agreements, spreadsheets, valuations systems, and memos without a common vocabulary or explicit links between each other. This paper develops a computational architecture for a persistent, evidence-backed representation of an investment whose accepted state, assumptions, sources, and computation rules are captured explicitly. The Investment Object is defined as a typed five-dimensional state including financial, contractual, risk, thesis, and evidence data, while the Financial State Dynamics Model (FSDM) is defined as a model controlling state transitions of the Investment Object, quantifying both unfavorable and favorable deviation from the investment thesis, and tracing changes propagation to dependent computations, financing, and tokens. The proposed system separates the AI-based interpretation of the data from deterministic computations and from the authorization process. A sample private-credit scenario is described in this paper as an illustration of the FSDM model: the reduction of the borrower's EBITDA from $50M to $40M impacts covenant headroom, loan valuation, the borrowing base of a fund, and a resulting liquidity gap. No empirical results are provided; only baseline experiments, metrics, and falsifiable hypotheses are proposed.

detail.abstract:
The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) has presented our legal system with a profound new dilemma. Public confidence in the capacity of AI to generate content is growing quickly, nearly apace with advancements in the technology itself. Yet, as AI-generated content masquerading as human-authored increasingly floods online platforms, our ability to tell the difference is diminishing. This widespread concealment of AI’s role in content creation has unleashed a cascade of harms for individuals as well as society at large. 

This Article exposes the law’s failure to regulate AI concealment, a legal vacuum that permits the proliferation of such concealment. To address this challenge, we must first theoretically interrogate why it is important to distinguish AI-generated content from human-authored works. Building on this theoretical foundation, we can then consider the feasibility of adopting a robust legal standard to regulate AI concealment. 

To this end, the Article advances a theory of “differentiated creativity.” This theory clarifies the fundamental differences between human creative processes—rooted in human intentionality, emotional expression, and control—and those of AI. Based on this theory, the Article then proposes “output transparency” as a new legal standard enabling clear differentiation between human and AI contributions.

To operationalize output transparency, the Article advocates two key legal reforms: requiring technology companies to watermark AI-generated content and obligating authors to provide proper explanations of the modifications they have made to such content. These proposed reforms would protect human adaptations of AI outputs, ensure a clear distinction between human and machine contributions, and enhance transparency across creative sectors. By implementing these reforms, the legal system can more effectively safeguard and foster the creative potential of both humans and AI, promoting balanced and ethical integration of technology in society.

detail.abstract: Can a statutory minimum-wage increase raise actual purchasing power without inducing job loss, informalization, lower hours, or consumer-price inflation when labor markets exhibit imperfect competition? We analyze 1,885,302 supplied Bolivian Continuous Employment Survey person-quarter records across 34 available quarterly files, city and category consumer-price indices, and the national legal wage path, contrasting competitive demand, monopsony and segmented labor adjustment. We distinguish nominal law, real full-time floor, worker earnings, a simultaneous negotiated wage provision, and each outcome's observational comparison. The 2025 nominal statutory increase of 10 percent was smaller than December-on-December inflation of 20.40 percent: the real legal minimum declined 8.64 percent. Among nine nonrandomly exposed departments, the baseline 2024Q4-2025Q4 differential employment gradient is-1.10 outcome percentage points per ten points greater predetermined wage-band exposure. The t 7-reference 95 percent interval is approximately [-6.07, 3.87] points, so a statistically indistinguishable zero is not proof of economic equivalence. Seven exposure constructions, eight fictitious wage thresholds, multiple timing windows, hours and response-coverage adjustments, age-sex cell standardization, 362,880 exact regional relabelings, and twelve price-division negative-control regressions uncover meaningful specification sensitivity and prior associations. The alternative 2023Q4 exposure vintage reverses the employment slope to +2.65 points, while a prior-window employment gradient reaches approximately-7.61 points. No 2025 price division survives family-wise Holm adjustment, but an earlier price placebo detects regional confounding. Substantial pension-item nonresponse rules out treating noncontribution among respondents as an official informal-employment rate. These outcomes are descriptive and adversarial assessments of a single national joint-policy episode, not identified nationwide causal treatment effects. Employer-linked data and valid external or quasi-experimental variation are needed to distinguish a causal monopsony correction from alternative adjustment mechanisms.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the impact of monetary policy variables on the performance of the stock market in Nigeria using quarterly data for twenty four years (1984:1-2007:4). A linear combination of stock market index and monetary policy variables is estimated using ordinary least squares; co-integration and error-correction specification. It is observed that stock market performance is strongly determined by broad money supply, exchange rates and consumer price index in the short and long-run. Hence, the liquidity, exchange rate and price level channel of monetary policy transmission is supported by evidence as determinants of stock price movements in Nigeria. On the other hand, minimum rediscount rate and treasury bill rates show mixed results, they were unable to demonstrate significant relationship to changes in stock market index, though their coefficients follow expectations. However, on a parsimonious examination of the variables, it is observed that a significant relationship exists if used discriminately. Hence, for the interest rate channel of monetary policy transmission to effect changes in stock market index either minimum rediscount rate or treasury bills rate should be applied at a time and not simultaneously.

detail.abstract: The banking industry has an important role in raising public funds, distributing financing, and supporting economic activities. In carrying out this role, banks need to maintain a balance between business growth, profitability, liquidity, asset quality, compliance, and customer trust. Competition with other banks and This study aims to analyze the performance of PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BNI) in 2025 from the perspective of performance management, by paying attention to financial results, target achievement, asset quality, efficiency, and strategic implications for the company's management. The research uses a qualitative descriptive method through a review of documents, especially the 2025 BNI Annual Report and performance information published by the company. The results of the analysis show that credit disbursements reached IDR 899.531 trillion or grew 15.9%, while third-party funds reached IDR 1,040.834 trillion. Gross NPL was recorded at 1.9%, better than 2.0% in 2024. On the other hand, net profit decreased from Rp21.464 trillion to Rp20.041 trillion, net interest margin decreased from 4.2% to 3.8%, and cost-to-income ratio increased from 44.6% to 46.5%. Thus, intermediation growth and asset quality are positive achievements, but profitability and efficiency are areas that need to be strengthened. This article recommends aligning key performance indicators with quality growth, process efficiency, customer experience, risk management, and employee competency development. The results of the analysis are expected to provide an overview that banking performance management needs to assess not only financial final results, but also processes and factors that support business sustainability.

detail.abstract: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) have become a central channel through which global capital interacts with Chinese mainland A-shares, Hong Kong-listed Chinese companies, and overseas Chinese concept stocks. Rather than treating “foreign capital” as a monolithic bloc, this paper analyzes FII ownership as a heterogeneous, regulation-embedded, and governance-relevant phenomenon. Drawing on agency theory, institutional theory, information asymmetry models, and capital market liberalization literature, the paper develops hypotheses on the characteristics of FII-held firms, the firm-level and macro-level determinants of FII ownership, and the consequences of FII presence for corporate governance, capital structure adjustment, innovation, performance, information efficiency, and market stability. The analysis emphasizes the Chinese context—QFII/RQFII, Stock Connect programs, Hong Kong as an offshore gateway, and US/HK-listed Chinese firms—while situating the discussion within the broader emerging-market literature. Expected results suggest that FIIs prefer large, liquid, transparent, and governance-strong firms; that FII ownership improves monitoring and valuation but with heterogeneous effects depending on investor horizon, identity, and ownership threshold; and that policy liberalization amplifies both the benefits and the vulnerabilities associated with foreign institutional capital.

detail.abstract: The statistical toolkit for backtest quality (the probability of backtest overfitting, the Deflated Sharpe Ratio, multiple-testing corrections, backtesting protocols) targets selection bias across many trials. Look-ahead bias, Sin #2 of the Deutsche Bank seven-sins taxonomy, has no comparable correction. By "deflator" we mean a specific object: an ex-post statistical correction, applied to reported performance numbers, that requires no rerun of the generating engine. No such correction can exist for timeline errors, because they are accounting errors, not sampling artifacts: statistics cannot repair a wrong timestamp. Operational corrections do exist (shift the fills and rerun), and we formalize both sides of that boundary. On a deliberately trivial daily crypto momentum strategy with zero parameter search, moving one line of timing code changes terminal wealth from 14.41x to 6,094.94x, a factor of 423, raises the Sharpe ratio from 1.01 to 2.81, and simultaneously reduces maximum drawdown from 44.7% to 18.9% on Bitcoin, 2017-2026. In this exhibit every headline metric an allocator screens on improves at once; the sign of the error is not guaranteed in general, and we show where it flips. The same error inflates terminal wealth 4,696x on ETHUSDT. We contribute: (i) decision/fill/credit-window semantics, three cleanliness conditions, and a seven-ledger taxonomy applied to identical position series; (ii) a proved flip-neighborhood identity for the wealth gap, plus its measured content: 261 log-basispoints per flip, with entry-day bars averaging +339 bps against +12 bps unconditionally; (iii) an experimental demonstration that purged walk-forward selection is silent on the error: honest out-of-sample diagnostics look unremarkable (Sharpe 0.81) while the same-bar ledger compounds 1,464x inside every fold; (iv) a four-test gate whose statistics are turnover-normalized and bootstrap-inferred, including an allocator-side correlation test runnable from position logs and public prices without the engine; and (v) a close-only S&P 500 exhibit reproducing the published equity pattern: the error converts a strategy that fails to beat the index (1.18x vs. 3.18x buy-and-hold) into one that appears to beat it (4.09x, Sharpe 2.12), at one-fifth the crypto per-flip intensity.

detail.abstract: This article retraces the history of the theory of non-competing groups and the occupational crowding hypothesis, two widely used concepts in the economic literature. We show that the two concepts share a common lineage and similarities. Using systematic bibliographic tracing, we analyze and compare their uses in the writings of J. S. Mill, J. E. Cairnes, M. G. Fawcett, F. Y. Edgeworth, F. W. Taussig, B. R. Bergmann, and W. A. Lewis. While the concept of non-competing groups was introduced to account for wage differentials caused by barriers to labor mobility in general, occupational crowding has mainly been used to explain racial and gender wage gaps. Our study identifies two distinct approaches to labor market segmentation, namely skill-stratifying groups and race-and/or gender-stratifying groups. The latter developed from the former as racial and gender issues entered economic analysis. The study sheds brighter light on the tension between priority of discovery and influence in the circulation of ideas. It also illustrates the challenges of attributing credit for scientific discoveries.

detail.abstract: Foreign-exchange intervention may affect retail inflation before it produces a large movement in average prices: it can change whether sellers reprice and in which direction. We study this margin using daily fuel-price reports from Peru and an out-of-sample innovation in official dollar sales. The innovation is the difference between realized sales and the prediction of a two-part central-bank reaction function estimated only with lagged public information and refitted through time. We aggregate daily innovations over each retail reporting interval and estimate local projections for the cumulative price, a price increase, a price decrease, and any adjustment. In the national sample, a one-standard-deviation innovation lowers the relative probability that liquid-fuel prices increase by 0.66 percentage points on impact and 0.69 percentage points after eight observation steps. The probability of any adjustment falls by 0.76 and 0.74 percentage points, respectively, while the decrease margin does not respond. The cumulative relative price effect emerges gradually and reaches-0.035 percent at step eight. Alternative reaction functions reproduce the adjustment-hazard results even when the price-level effect is less stable. Unexpected intervention is therefore associated primarily with fewer upward resets and more inaction, not with a mechanical substitution toward price cuts. The findings identify the direction and frequency of repricing as a distinct margin of foreign-exchange-policy transmission.

detail.abstract: Latency arbitrage in retail foreign exchange and CFD markets exploits the interval during which a broker's displayed quote lags a faster reference price. Practitioner sources describe this interval with loose ranges such as 50-200 ms, and the peer-reviewed evidence concerns equities at microsecond scales. This paper measures the interval directly. Using tick recordings of XAUUSD from three sessions at three anonymised retail brokers, each paired with a fast reference feed on a single recording clock, we define stale-quote windows by a cross-side gap threshold and measure their duration exactly within the recording. At a 30-point (0.30 USD) threshold the brokers showed 240 to 824 windows per hour, with median durations of 34 to 56 ms; between 22% and 35% of windows closed within 20 ms and between 19% and 31% remained open beyond 100 ms. A simulated order arriving 30 ms after the signal and closed one second later would have captured a mean gross result of +22, +12 and +2 points on displayed quotes, against −9, −12 and −49 points for random entries. The delay at which the mean result reaches zero ranges from about 40 ms to beyond 150 ms, depending mainly on quote update frequency and spread. A second reference feed produced 4.6 times as many windows but almost no edge, showing that window counts are not a measure of opportunity. Results are reproduced on a second, independently produced export of the same recording. The data contain displayed quotes only, so all results are gross upper bounds.

detail.abstract: Law that addresses work-related mental suffering is typically built around an individual event: a claimant, a diagnosis, a causal link, a foreseeable injury. Exhaustion in high-volume public institutions is produced and sustained differently, through routines, metrics and habits of silence that no single decision-maker authors. This article asks whether this mismatch of analytical unit helps explain why the exhaustion of judicial workforces becomes legally visible late and incompletely, and what a literary figure, the haunted courthouse, contributes to seeing it. The method is doctrinal and comparative analysis of Brazil, England and Wales, France, and Germany and the European Union, together with descriptive use of official Brazilian judicial statistics and selective interdisciplinary literature on burnout, institutional betrayal and street-level bureaucracy. The premise of the Brazilian novel O Prédio que Aprendeu a Escutar is read as a heuristic, never as evidence. The article advances, as a doctrinal and normative proposition rather than an empirical finding, that individual-event regimes (Sutherland v Hatton; Brazilian occupational-disease adjudication) and organizational regimes (the French France Télécom convictions; Brazil's NR-1 psychosocial-risk amendments) operate unevenly, and that Brazilian magistrates and statutory servants sit at the margin of the organizational regime because NR-1's textual scope turns on employment under the CLT. It proposes an organizational-unit reading of duties already contained in CNJ Resolutions 207/2015 and 351/2020, comprising unit-level indicators and a documented duty to respond, justified by analogy with the hearing norm that courts apply to litigants. Limitations include dependence on aggregate data and a single literary text.

detail.abstract: Jean-Baptiste Say is often described as a theorist of laissez faire and minimal government. This article argues that such a view overlooks the key role he assigned to the "public economy." It reconstructs the meaning, scope, and implications of this notion, with particular attention to his analysis of public goods, which he termed "public consumptions." I establish that Say put forward some of the earliest and clearest accounts of non-excludability, non-rivalry, and free riding, thereby anticipating criteria and examples-such as national defense, the lighthouse, scientific research, and certain natural resources-that would later become standard in the modern literature. He also developed early formulations of the benefit principle of taxation as both a distributive principle-tying fiscal contributions to the advantages afforded by public goods-and an efficiency criterion requiring that benefits at least offset costs. In Say's framework, public goods enhance productive capacities; their provision addresses identifiable market failures and underpins a coherent rationale for government intervention. Say's public economy is thus not an alternative to the private economy, but both its necessary extension and its complement. This dual characterization reflects the subtlety and complexity of Say's thought and is best regarded as an expression of his practical political economy.

detail.abstract: This paper interrogates whether competition law can carry distributive obligations without surrendering its analytical discipline. Kenya and South Africa answer differently. Kenya's Competition Act 2010 gestures at public interest in merger review. South Africa's Competition Act 1998, as amended in 2018, writes employment and a greater spread of ownership into the test for every merger. Both operate beneath constitutions that guarantee consumers' rights, food, housing and social security, subject to progressive realisation. The paper argues that the supposed conflict between consumer welfare, employment security and ownership transformation is misconceived, because each is a separate instrument for realizing one constitutional promise: access to a dignified economic life. It develops a three-ledger model and a rights-nexus test that discipline distributive conditions through causation, proportionality and durability. Evidence from Massmart, the Canal+ and Coca-Cola mergers, and labour data showing 33.6 per cent unemployment in South Africa and 83.8 per cent informality in Kenya, tests the model. The paper concludes that Kenya's informal economy, rather than its merger docket, is where distributive competition law must be built, and that South Africa's ownership agenda survives only if its conditions are made verifiable by regulators and courts alike. The argument is tested against live merger practice.

detail.abstract: Population aging and fertility decline are occurring simultaneously worldwide, straining labor supply and pension systems. China began a gradual delayedretirement (GDR) reform in 2025, raising statutory retirement ages on different schedules for men, female cadres, and female workers across birth cohorts. To evaluate its effects on older individuals and within the family, we develop a model of older adults' retirement, intergenerational transfers, and adult children's fertility decisions, with parameters estimated via fuzzy regression discontinuity at the pre-2025 statutory retirement ages. Counterfactual simulations show that, for mature reform cohorts, the GDR reform increases older employment and monetary transfers to adult children but reduces grandparental childcare. Because the reduction in childcare outweighs the increase in monetary transfers, fertility and older adults' welfare decline, with particularly large losses among lower-income women. Fully flexible retirement, mandatory partial retirement, and mandatory full-time work do not raise employment without similarly reducing fertility and welfare. Childcare subsidies can offset the declines in fertility and welfare, while restricting eligibility to women or lower-income women requires higher subsidy rates but reduces average fiscal expenditure. These findings suggest that evaluations of retirement policy should consider not only its direct effects on older adults' labor supply, but also its fertility effects through intergenerational transfers; childcare support can help mitigate these negative intergenerational effects of delayed retirement.

detail.abstract: Financial news headlines emphasize selected aspects of a broader story. We study the pricing implications of this choice by comparing published headlines with counterfactual headline distributions generated from the same articles using large language models. detail.abstract:
Global food supply chain vulnerabilities necessitate active refrigeration alternatives, yet
contemporary literature fails to bridge physical packaging heat-transfer boundaries with multi-
commodity biochemical preservation kinetics. To address this research gap, this study develops a
unified in silico multiphysics modeling framework to optimize and quantify the preservation
efficacy of passive, bio-based Phase Change Material (PCM) packaging systems during transit
failure.
Using an empirical meta-analysis research design, secondary thermodynamic and kinetic datasets
were extracted from an 16-paper high-impact literature cohort to model a continuous 48-hour
transport window. The analytical approach coupled transient container energy balances with
zero/first-order Arrhenius decay equations and dynamic, temperature-dependent modified
Gompertz growth models across six targeted matrices: Tomatoes, Leafy Greens, Fresh Poultry,
Pasteurized Milk, Frozen Pork Slabs, and Mackerel.
Numerical integration trials revealed that unmitigated temperature abuse (25°C control)
precipitated rapid multi-commodity quality or microbial collapse, breaching critical regulatory
safety thresholds within a narrow window of 8.2 to 19.7 hours. Conversely, incorporating a shape-
𝜅=0.20 W/m . K  ∆Hm=180 kJ/kg
stabilized nanoparticle/biopolymer PCM matrix (𝜅 = 0.20 W/m . K ; ∆𝐻𝑚 = 180 kJ/kg) flatlined
internal microclimates, successfully delaying decay rate constants and arresting hazardous
Enterobacter aerogenes proliferation and histamine toxin accumulation below the FDA hazard
threshold (50 mg/100g).
These findings bridge the gap between materials science and food biology by demonstrating how
optimized physical attributes physically control mathematical reaction velocities, firmly
supporting predictive bio-preservation theories. Ultimately, these calculated Shelf-Life Extension
Factors (2.44 to 5.88) validate that sustainable, passive bio-PCMs can entirely replace energy-
intensive active refrigeration across short-haul distribution networks to secure global food
security margins.

detail.abstract:
Governance has become more codified, more audited, and more comprehensively scored with each decade since the Cadbury Report of 1992. Governance failure has not become correspondingly rarer. This paper argues that the paradox persists not because governance measurement fails, but because it commits a category error about what measurement can do. Governance scoring evaluates the condition of a governance system at a point in time. It does not, and structurally cannot, interpret the trajectory of that system. The empirical record supports the distinction rather than merely asserting it: commercial governance ratings have been shown not to predict the outcome their vendors claim they predict, and the divergence among environmental, social and governance (ESG) rating providers arises chiefly from measurement rather than from disagreement about what matters.

The paper proposes Fragility Intelligence as an interpretive discipline distinct from governance scoring, and locates it precisely withinfive established traditionsthatbit inherits from ratherthan displaces: the strategic warning tradition runningfrom Wohlstetter through Grabo to the currencycrisis signals literature; the quantitative failure predictiontraditionof Altman, Beneish and Dechow, which already performs part of the function claimed here and performs it well; the organisational failure traditionof Turner, Vaughn, Perrow and Rasmussen; the institutionaldecoupling traditionof Meyer and Rowanand the audit ritual critique of Power; and the attentionand silence tradition of Ocasio, Morrison and Milliken, extended to the literature on cohesion and organisationalcorruption. It also situates itself in relation to Taleb, from whom it inherits the term, and to the cybernetic tradition of Ashby and Beer. The contribution claimed is narrow and therefore defensible. Fragility Intelligence shifts the unit of analysis from control to the interpretive capacity of the governance tier, imports a formal warning cycle into a domain that has never had one, and couples detection to an explicit transmission theory.

The paper states a formal definition, declares scope conditions and boundary limits, and advances nine falsifiable propositions with explicit falsification conditions: six about the discipline and three about the architecture through which it operates. That architecture is the principal addition in this version. Because the available evidence, stated as Proposition 6 and extended by Proposition 7, indicates that institutional failure is predominantly a failure of response rather than of detection, the paper sets out the principles of an escalation architecture in which the reporting channel is itself measured, the obstruction of a signal is registered as a signal in its own right, and escalation is judged by whether custody of a concern leaves the control of the people it concerns, not by how many levels it climbs. The paper also identifies an unexamined consequence: a functioning fragility intelligence capability materially alters directors' oversight liability under the Caremark line of authority, satisfying the first prong of the doctrine while manufacturing evidence for the second, and it can supply the evidence a South African governing body needs to substantiate its concluding statement on governance outcomes under the King V Code on Corporate Governance for South Africa, 2025 (King V). The paper closes by naming the five most serious threats to its own research programme, including the risk that its doctrine has run ahead of its evidence.

title: Trade Shocks, Currency Unions and the Role of Fiscal Transfers
affiliations: Boston University

detail.title: Trade Shocks, Currency Unions and the Role of Fiscal Transfers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the research presented in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: A common trade shock can affect members of a currency union differently, while monetary policy cannot respond separately to country-specific conditions. This paper studies whether cross-country fiscal transfers can substitute for this missing adjustment margin. I develop a dynamic quantitative trade model featuring nominal rigidities and heterogeneous households, which I apply to the 2025 U.S. tariff shock in the euro area. I introduce a cross-country fiscal transfer rule that operates as an automatic stabilizer, directing resources toward countries more adversely affected by the shock. Fiscal transfers of less than 1% of euro-area GDP in present value offset all the additional dispersion in terms of involuntary unemployment and consumption generated by the loss of country-specific monetary policy, while reducing a sizable part of the additional dispersion in employment. Thus, relatively small cross-country transfers can substitute for much of the stabilization role of country-specific monetary policy. Finally, I show that euro-area retaliation combined with fiscal transfers would have further mitigated the labor-market effects of the U.S. tariff shock.

affiliations.org_name: Unaffiliated Authors - affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract:
White collar crimes such as bank fraud, insider trading, corruption, money laundering and
corporate fraud cause great damage to the economy. Still, society often treats them lightly.
India has many laws against these crimes, and the list keeps growing. The main ones are the
Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA), the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988,
the Companies Act, 2013, the SEBI Act, 1992 and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS).
Even so, big scams like the Harshad Mehta scam, the Satyam fraud and the PNB–Nirav Modi
fraud show that enforcement is still weak in practice.

This paper asks one main question: is the problem in the law or in the way the law is enforced?
It argues that India has enough laws, but enforcement is weak because many agencies work
separately, trials are slow, convictions are few and political influence is feared. At the same
time, some powers given to the agencies are so strict that they can harm the rights of the
accused. The paper studies the main laws, the work of the agencies, important Supreme Court
judgments and the approach of other countries. It ends with suggestions to make enforcement
stronger and fairer.

title: The Crisis that did not Come: Explaining Fiscal Populism without Collapse in Israel, 2009-2025
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Crisis that did not Come: Explaining Fiscal Populism without Collapse in Israel, 2009-2025

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is Chief Economic Commentator at Calcalist, an Israeli financial newspaper, and writes regularly on Israeli economic policy. This research was conducted independently; Calcalist had no role in it, and the views expressed are solely those of the author.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study uses publicly available documents and data and involves no human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Between 2009 and 2025, with the exception of 2021-2022, Israeli fiscal policy satisfied the operational criteria of fiscal populism under the Dornbusch-Edwards framework. Yet the predicted macroeconomic crisis never materialized, despite fifteen years of fiscal populism and two system-wide shocks, the second a war that pushed the fiscal deficit above 8% of GDP. This paper explains that anomaly through three structural buffers: a knowledge-intensive export sector, a domestic institutional investor base, and an independent and credible central bank, which together blocked the crisis channels running from fiscal populism to macroeconomic crisis. The paper then asks why the same governments preserved these buffers while eroding the institutions that normally constrain fiscal populism. It argues that this pattern reflects Functional Selectivity: institutions were treated according to whether their alteration bears on one of the three crisis channels. The Bennett-Lapid government (2021-2022) serves as a within-case control separating political choice from structural constraint. Over time, however, this resilience generated a dynamic cost. By absorbing shocks, the buffers suppressed the contemporaneous signals of foundation erosion, allowing it to continue without correction. This Masking Effect gives rise to Self-Undermining Resilience, whereby the very mechanisms that prevent crisis gradually weaken the conditions on which they depend. The Israeli case does not refute the Dornbusch-Edwards framework; it identifies the boundary conditions under which fiscal populism can persist without the predicted crisis.

detail.abstract: Property taxpayers often assume that rising assessed values automatically allow local governments to collect more property tax revenue. That intuition fits rate-driven taxes such as sales taxes, but it is less appropriate in property tax systems where local governments choose the levy and the tax rate is calculated afterward. This paper estimates how responsive local government property tax levies are to changes in the property tax base in Cook County, Illinois, from 2008 through 2023. Using data on municipalities, school districts, townships, and other taxing agencies, we find that annual changes in equalized assessed value are far more volatile than annual changes in levies. In the pooled descriptive data, tax base changes are negative in more than half of agency-year observations, while levy declines occur in less than one quarter of observations. OLS estimates show positive but small contemporaneous elasticities: a 10 percent increase in the tax base is associated with less than a 1 percent increase in the levy in the preferred pooled specifications. Instrumental variables estimates that use reassessment timing to isolate variation in the tax base are smaller and often statistically indistinguishable from zero. We also test for asymmetric and lagged responses. Evidence for asymmetry is limited and sensitive to specification, while OLS models provide some evidence of lagged responses, especially for school districts. Overall, the results suggest that in this levy-first institutional setting, changes in the property tax base do not translate into large contemporaneous changes in local government levies. The findings clarify an important distinction in property tax politics: reassessments can redistribute the tax burden across taxpayers without mechanically increasing total revenue collected by local governments.
