detail.abstract: Computational framing analysis has been dominated by supervised classification methods requiring large annotated corpora and predefined frame taxonomies, limiting their applicability to non-English languages, novel events, and resource-scarce contexts. This paper presents Association Rule Mining (ARM) as an unsupervised, annotation-free framework for news framing detection, addressed to interdisciplinary venues spanning computational media studies, data journalism, and communication research. The primary validation is the Framing Gaza project: 25,512 English-language news articles from 16 outlets across the United States, United Kingdom, France, and Germany, covering the first year of the Gaza war (October 2023 to October 2024). ARM (Apriori algorithm, mlxtend) is applied to headlines and body text with platform-weighted support calculation (weights of 1/√(n) per outlet), POS-filtered n-gram preprocessing, and liftbased framing distinctiveness scoring. Results demonstrate that ARM inductively surfaces interpretable framing patterns without predefined categories. A platform-level closed-rule analysis across all 16 outlets identifies the West Bank triple cluster ({bank, west, israeli}) as the most structurally robust cross-platform co-occurrence (a marker of topical salience rather than, in itself, a frame), present as a closed rule in all 16 outlets (lift 58.3, confidence 97.8%), and {israeli, strike} to {kill} as the dominant military frame in 14 of 16 outlets (lift 8.7, confidence 56.5%). A temporal analysis of body-text closed rules across 12 consecutive months shows event-driven framing pivots without prior event labeling: the World Central Kitchen strike of April 2024 produces the most tightly bound n-gram cluster of any single-event month (lift 6.43), and geographic frames shift from Khan Younis (January 2024, peak lift 6.67) to West Bank (July 2024) to Lebanon-ceasefire (September 2024) in correspondence with documented operational phases. A systematic headline-body framing divergence is identified: headline framing is editorially constructed, while body text is dominated by institutional and procedural language. As a methodological validation study, the paper additionally reports on the Seven Days project, where the framework was tested under acute conditions using FP-Growth on Arabic-language coverage of the 2026 Iran war (1,575 articles, 5 outlets, 10-day window), demonstrating that replacing Apriori with FP-Growth enables sentencelevel transaction analysis with substantially reduced memory overhead, while producing comparable framing patterns. All findings were validated through editorial partnership: two published investigative stories, on Daraj Media and Saheeh Masr, developed by independent editorial teams. Preprocessing code is released openly; the full ARM pipeline is documented but not released to preserve the framework's operational deployability.

title: Ecological Belonging and the Economics of Climate Change
affiliations: Universidad Metropolitana -

detail.title: Ecological Belonging and the Economics of Climate Change

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interest
declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract: Climate change reveals a mismatch between humanity’s material and biological dependence on a shared Earth system and the institutional boundaries governing production, consumption, investment, and political accountability. This article extends the Philosophy of Belonging through its mature Ethics of Belonging, distinguishing constitutive ecological dependence from adequate institutional belonging. It argues that climate change is not only an externality or coordination failure but also a potential failure of collective adaptability: present prosperity may undermine the ecological conditions and distributed human capacities required for future development. Four ontological principles—constitutive integration, imperfect belonging, stratified reality, and dual temporality—organize the analysis. Three scientifically revisable conditions of adequate social ethics—developing constituent belonging needs, enabling initiative and participation, and orienting decisions toward the great community—provide criteria for investigating climate institutions. Individual ethics and six interacting psychological developmental steps explain possible pathways from embodied and emotional life to reflective ecological agency. The framework is compared with externality theory, integrated assessment, ecological economics, commons governance, environmental justice, and capability theory. A policy architecture and nine testable propositions connect emissions reduction, social inclusion, economic transformation, and adaptive governance. The article proposes a conceptual research program, not a new climate-damage estimate or an unconditional moral deduction.

detail.abstract: The direction of technical change-Harrod-, Hicks-or Solow-neutral-is often read as a finding but constructed as a representation. The accounts register each factor only as an engine, the product of a count and an efficiency index; a designation of units divides the engine's growth between accumulation and augmentation. A classification is a representation when the convention defining the units, not the technology, sets that division; a hypothesis when natural units, measured in form and function and counting capital and labor by the same attribute, frame it; and a finding when, in addition, independent data agree. Counting capital in dollars makes its index constant by construction, so the purely labor-augmenting reading is a representation; counting labor in wage units makes it capital-augmenting. Recent growth theory has met contrary evidence with mechanisms that keep capital counted in dollars; this paper examines that premise. No classification has yet become a finding, the requirement for full validation.

detail.abstract: Why firms pay dividends has been debated for a century. This paper reviews that debate around one question: what does a dividend do that retained earnings or a share repurchase cannot? Tracing the answer from the 1930s to the evidence produced since 2010, including recent work on social responsibility, climate risk and supervisory payout restrictions, we argue that much of the puzzle posed by Black in 1976 has been dissolved and that the evidence supports a commitment view of the dividend, provided that observed rigidity and the cost of breaking a payout promise are measured separately. The same evidence opens a new puzzle. Repurchases made under formal programmes have become nearly as rigid as dividends, and the two instruments are not close substitutes. We conjecture that each commits the firm to a different audience, compare it with the main rival accounts and derive five predictions, with designs that could reject it. The conjecture is not tested here. The agenda gives particular attention to controlled firms, emerging markets, climate shocks and the financing of investment in artificial intelligence.

detail.abstract: This study revisits the finance-growth nexus in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), a highly dollarized economy characterized by shallow financial intermediation and limited access to credit. Using a Granger causality framework, the analysis examines the direction of causality between financial development and economic growth. The results provide little support for the Supply-Leading Hypothesis: private sector credit and monetary depth do not Granger-cause economic growth. Conversely, economic growth significantly Granger-causes private sector credit, providing evidence in favor of the Demand-Following Hypothesis. These findings suggest that, at the current stage of development, the Congolese financial system remains more responsive to real economic expansion than capable of independently driving it. From a development-finance perspective, the results imply that financial deepening alone may be insufficient to generate sustainable growth without complementary improvements in productive investment, infrastructure, human capital, institutional quality, innovation, and financial inclusion. The long-term policy challenge is therefore to foster a transition from a Demand-Following regime toward a Feedback regime in which financial development and economic growth become mutually reinforcing.

title: Why the Last Trade Is the Wrong Price: Measuring Favorite-Longshot Bias on Kalshi
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Why the Last Trade Is the Wrong Price: Measuring Favorite-Longshot Bias on Kalshi

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I declare no competing interests. I have no financial or personal relationship with Kalshi or any other organization that could have influenced this study.

detail.abstract: Many betting markets show a favorite-longshot bias: long shots win less often than their prices say, and favorites win a little more often. I tested for it on Kalshi, a U.S. prediction market, using 26,192 settled markets on sports games and daily weather. My first approach used each market's last trade before it closed. It showed a huge bias. Only 16 of the 17,612 markets in the lowest price range won, against about 229 expected. But this turned out to be a measurement error. Game markets stay open until the game ends, so the last trade comes when the winner is already known. Prices also can't go below one cent. I then repeated the test using prices from before the outcome was known. On 810 MLB games in 2026, underdogs won 40.6% of the time against an average price of 42.6%. That gap of 2.0 percentage points goes the expected way, but it's too small to tell apart from chance (p = 0.24). On 4,000 fifteen-minute Bitcoin markets, prices measured inside the trading window were close to the actual win rates, and the gaps were small and inconsistent from one measurement time to the next. My results don't show a bias that could be traded. They do show how easily a measurement choice can create one.

detail.abstract:
Background: Late-career employment may lower risk of later-life Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD).

Methods: We examined late-career employment, ages 55-67, and subsequent ADRD risk between ages 70-85, in a nationwide population cohort (n=613,983), a population-based HUNT Study-cohort (n=8,037), and their ADRD-discordant siblings (population, n=17,580, HUNT, n=270), as well as a HUNT-non-participant cohort (n=8,395). Employment was from prospective national registries, ADRD diagnoses, health, and lifestyle factors from national registries and study-specific HUNT assessments. The cohorts’ selection and detection biases were evaluated, and bias-corrected estimates calculated. Logistic and conditional regression, sensitivity analyses with early-mid-adult health and lifestyle factors, complete data, robustness, and sociodemographic heterogeneity analyses were performed.

Findings: After correcting for detection and selection biases, 13 years of full-- and part-time employment were associated with ~37% lower odds of ADRD in both cohorts. Full-time employment for half the time, 6·5 years, was linked to 19% lower odds of ADRD. Odds ratios for late career employment on subsequent ADRD risk were consistent across all models, and slightly lower in the ADRD-discordant sibling cohorts, suggesting a likely causal relationship. A one-year increase in late-career employment was estimated to reduce ADRD prevalence in the population aged 70-85 by 2·6%.

Interpretation: ​Our results were robust across cohorts and analyses, suggesting an extended window of opportunity for ADRD risk reduction through employment, even part-time, adding working in late-career to potential intervention targets.

detail.abstract: What drives business cycles in Rio Grande do Sul (RS), a highly indebted Brazilian state? We answer this question with a regional DSGE model that separates local from federal fiscal policy, includes public capital, and allows for hand-tomouth households. RS fluctuations are driven mainly by tax, productivity and household preference shocks. Government spending and monetary policy matter little, and fiscal multipliers are below one. The model tracks the path of RS output and the comovement between output and wages. It overstates the volatility of wages and inflation, however, and misses the countercyclical behavior of federal spending.

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence increasingly determines not only which expression individuals encounter, but how that expression is selected, sequenced, personalized, reinforced, and distributed through adaptive computational systems. This paper examines when such routing mechanisms may become legally relevant to imminent unlawful-action analysis without weakening the constitutional protections established by Brandenburg v. Ohio.

The paper distinguishes static algorithmic curation from adaptive AI routing and introduces Action-Conversion Routing as a proposed diagnostic category for examining specific pathways through which protected expression may become connected to imminent unlawful conduct. It identifies the Doctrinal Clouding Zone, where prediction, optimization, behavioral feedback, and pathway reinforcement complicate established distinctions among protected advocacy, editorial discretion, intermediary liability, and legally attributable conduct.

To address these questions, the manuscript develops a six-factor evidentiary framework, a four-tier operator-responsibility classification, and methods for reconstructing and testing disputed routing pathways. Drawing upon Brandenburg, Moody v. NetChoice, Twitter v. Taamneh, Section 230, and governing evidentiary principles, it distinguishes technical capability from demonstrated operation, exposure from causation, and foreseeability from legally sufficient intent.

The framework creates neither a new incitement offense nor an independent basis for liability. It preserves lawful advocacy, expressive editorial discretion, viewpoint neutrality, and existing constitutional thresholds while advancing a disciplined method for examining adaptive communications architecture.

The paper’s central proposition is preservationist: the future of free speech does not require weakening Brandenburg. It requires understanding the architecture through which speech now moves.

detail.abstract: A large majority of the well-known governance indicators are based on the opinions of external experts. However, they fail to capture how citizens perceive the governance environment and outcomes in their countries. This paper discusses the advantages of a uniform and consistent framework for measuring governance quality across countries and over time based on evaluations by citizens, and the related challenges. We implement this framework in practice using data from the World Values Surveys and provide a worldwide ranking of countries based on how citizens perceive the governance quality in their own countries. We further discuss how to correct the resulting citizen-centric governance indicators for biases that could potentially be present in public opinion surveys, and the possible use of these indicators in policy making.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the Greek balancing market in combination with the Day-Ahead Market (DAM) for September 2026, explaining how Uplift Accounts 2 and 3 (UA2, UA3) are affected. The analysis is based on a comparison of 15-minute public data from IPTO, HEnEx, ENTSO-E, and RAAEY; the cross-border notices of JAO; and the Balancing Market Rulebook.

The cost of UA2 and UA3 is concentrated in two windows of the same day (midday and the evening ramp), which operate through different mechanisms. At midday, characterized by a RES surplus and zero or negative DAM prices, UA3 is loaded (~37.5 €/MWh), because the upward energy of the Integrated Scheduling Process (ISP) is not recovered through the imbalance price, which settles at the floor of −100 €/MWh. In the evening ramp, by contrast, UA2 is loaded (~10.4 €/MWh) because of the cost of reserve capacity. Security redispatch is the component with the largest effect on UA3. In the week 21–27 September, the midday UA3 rose with the INTERV_GE security constraints, from 8 €/MWh on days with 0–100 MW of constraints to 52–67 €/MWh on days with 607–734 MW, including 26 September, when the DAM price was positive and there was no surplus in the DAM. Valued at the marginal upward mFRR price, security energy amounted to about €19.3 million over 31 August–27 September, about 20% of the official UA3; the actual amount may differ, because this energy is paid at each unit's bid price, which is not published. The study also shows that lower demand raises both accounts per MWh, because the same cost is spread over fewer MWh, and that reduced export NTCs, which are binding at midday, add to the surplus that remains in the domestic market.

Finally, the inflation of UA2 and UA3 is assessed to be mainly structural, as participants respond rationally to the market rules, and specific policy proposals are presented. The paper is based on descriptive analysis, not on a market simulation.

detail.abstract: This study constructs a linked dataset connecting U.S. federal patent opinions to litigated patents and extracted damages signals over 2005-2025. From 420 damages-relevant opinions, 103 mention "reasonable royalty" and 34 articulate an explicit numeric reasonable royalty amount. Articulated awards are highly concentrated (mean $33.19M; median $477k; skewness 4.72; Gini 0.855). Reasonable royalty mention is associated with substantially higher likelihood of numeric articulation (35.1% vs 5.5%), and with greater patent bundling (mean patents per case 1.35 vs 0.61). Within a valuation-signal subset (n=45), market-referential indicators appear more frequently than income-or cost-based indicators. The results describe the structure of publicly observable judicial valuation signals and clarify the limits of inference from articulated awards alone.

detail.abstract: Standards-based industries are governed by layered institutional processes in which technological innovation, intellectual property commitments, and product-market realization unfold under partially coordinated but distinct mechanisms. Yet empirical analyses rarely integrate these dimensions within a single framework. This analysis develops a three-layer empirical model linking technology-proximate patent intensity, institutional consolidation through IEEE Letters of Assurance (LOAs), and ecosystem diffusion measured through Wi-Fi Alliance certified product adoption. Using successive IEEE 802.11 generations-Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac), Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax), Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be), and Wi-Fi Aware (802.11aq/NAN)-we examine how innovation persistence, institutional participation, and category-level diffusion interact over time. The findings suggest that persistence of innovation activity, measured via patent pulse width, predicts ecosystem breadth more strongly than peak patent intensity. Institutional consolidation, measured via LOA concentration (HHI), evolves dynamically and does not uniformly precede diffusion. Platform-generational technologies display sustained multi-category diffusion, while feature-layer amendments exhibit narrow adoption despite strong innovation pulses. The analysis contributes an institutional governance perspective on technological trajectories, emphasizing sequencing, commitment dispersion, and certification coordination as measurable determinants of ecosystem realization in standards-intensive industries.

detail.abstract: As innovation systems evolve toward greater architectural complexity, standards dependence, and distributed value creation, intellectual property (IP) increasingly operates as a system-level component rather than a standalone economic asset. In such environments, IP valuation is frequently performed at stages where the asset’s technical role and its downstream institutional and economic treatment remain unresolved. Despite the consistent application of established valuation methodologies, resulting value estimates often diverge substantially, creating ambiguity for investment, governance, and strategic decision-making. Such divergence is not anomalous, nor attributable to methodological error; it reflects a structural measurement gap within contemporary innovation systems. Prevailing valuation models implicitly assume bounded usage contexts, interpretable claim relevance, and stable monetization pathways. These assumptions routinely fail in emerging and standards-driven technologies, where system architecture, standards alignment, and institutional outcomes evolve asynchronously. As a result, valuation outputs primarily encode sensitivity to unresolved system conditions rather than stable economic signals. The paper identifies the absence of an explicit pre-valuation interpretability layer to characterize how valuation outputs should be interpreted under unresolved system conditions as a missing measurement layer in current innovation infrastructure. By reframing valuation divergence as a system-level observability problem, this work positions the explicit articulation of valuation assumptions as a necessary antecedent to economic valuation. The argument is developed through innovation system evolution, the structural limits of valuation under system fluidity, and the implications for standards governance and future technology measurement frameworks.

detail.abstract: Educational expansion changes how dispersed schooling is in each generation, and the intergenerational elasticity of education moves with that dispersion. This paper asks how much of the variation in the elasticity across countries, census rounds, and regions of Latin America and the Caribbean reflects dispersion rather than how strongly a parent's position predicts the child's. Using 96 censuses from 23 countries, I measure positional persistence with schooling demeaned by birth cohort and sex, ranked, and converted to normal scores, and I decompose differences in the elasticity exactly into positional, dispersion, and measurement components. The ratio of children's to parents' dispersion follows the hump-shaped relation between mean schooling and its dispersion, so each country's stage of expansion predicts it. Across countries, the Pearson correlation of raw schooling removes most of the dispersion component. Over time, dispersion accounts for a median of 62 percent of the change in the elasticity, and in four countries positional persistence rose significantly while the elasticity fell. Across the parental distribution, persistence is weakest among children of the least-educated parents.

detail.abstract: Motivated by the fact that recessions vary substantially in their recovery dynamics both across time and across states, we develop a simple, transparent, and flexible algorithm that classifies each recession as either U-shaped, with sufficiently strong post-trough growth, or L-shaped, exhibiting weaker recoveries. In addition to the shape classification, our approach also yields a recession-specific measure of recovery strength. Applying our approach to the Philadelphia Fed's state coincident indices over 1979-2025, we document substantial heterogeneity in both the shape and strength of recoveries. State-level recessions are better described as a mix of U and L-shaped dynamics rather than as uniformly U-shaped or L-shaped episodes, with the relative importance of the two components varying across states and recession episodes. These findings are broadly validated when using state-level real GDP and are robust to alternative recovery classifications, horizons, and recession-dating methods. We also find considerable heterogeneity in synchronization with the national business cycle, with stronger comovement among Heartland states and more idiosyncratic dynamics among oil-producing states. Regression results further show that the determinants of recovery shape and recovery strength differ. Aggregate and regional conditions are more strongly associated with the likelihood that a recession is U-shaped, whereas the recovery strength conditional on the existence of a distinct recovery stage is more systematically associated with state-level characteristics. This distinction between the extensive and intensive recovery margins is particularly evident for manufacturing, which is associated with a lower probability of a recovery but stronger recoveries when such growth occurs.

detail.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer significant potential for automating causal analysis of nuclear Licensee Event Reports (LERs), yet their tendency to generate plausible but unsupported causal claims-termed causal hallucination-poses serious risks in safetycritical regulatory contexts where traceability and factual grounding are mandatory. This study proposes and evaluates a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework designed to constrain LLM causal inference to evidence explicitly present in the LER corpus. Building upon the hybrid causality extraction framework and its 20,129-sample LER corpus, we construct a vector-indexed retrieval layer that supplies the model with semantically relevant report passages prior to causal relation generation. We systematically quantify causal hallucination using a novel benchmark distinguishing three error types: fabricated causal links, unsupported causal directionality, and over-generalized causal claims. Experiments compare a baseline instruction-tuned LLM against three RAG configurations (dense retrieval, hybrid sparsedense retrieval, and retrieval with reranking) across detection accuracy, extraction fidelity, and hallucination rate. Results are validated against expert-annotated causeeffect pairs and assessed for citation faithfulness-whether each generated causal claim is traceable to a retrieved source span. We further analyze failure modes where retrieval fails to surface implicit causal evidence, and propose a confidence-gated abstention mechanism that defers to human review when retrieval support is weak. The findings aim to establish measurable reliability criteria for LLM-assisted causal analysis in nuclear safety, offering a replicable methodology for grounding generative models in verifiable operating experience data.

detail.abstract: We develop a unified method for assessing local equilibrium determinacy and computing impulse responses in continuous-time heterogeneous-agent models. A forward-backward decomposition of linearized equilibrium dynamics separates stable adjustments propagated forward from components determined by future shocks and infinite-horizon admissibility. Matching these components to inherited states characterizes existence and uniqueness and determines the response when it is unique. Our central constructive result obtains this decomposition from household response operators and market-clearing price feedback. Starting from a known fixed-price household split, we use the response factors underlying fake news kernel and small price-consistency solves to construct the equilibrium stable and unstable projections. This construction makes the common determinacy and solution mechanism operational without requiring a full equilibrium eigendecomposition. The same projections supply an exact continuation condition for a stationary infinite tail, removing time-horizon truncation error.

detail.abstract: Financial regulation increasingly governs artificial intelligence (AI) through frameworks that address models, data, system life cycles and human oversight. Agentic AI creates a distinct regulatory problem when institutions delegate consequential decision-making and execution authority to artificial agents. This paper develops the delegated autonomy gap (DAG), defined as a material misalignment between the form and scope of delegated machine authority and the governance capacities available to structure and control its exercise. Drawing on structured documentary analysis of 27 regulatory and policy documents published by 31 August 2026, the paper examines regulatory constructions of machine authority across financial settings. It identifies five constitutive dimensions of action governance capacity: mandate, permissioning, boundaries, observability, and intervention and contestability. The paper situates the DAG within scholarship on regulatory delegation, meta-regulation, accountability infrastructures, algorithmic governance and meaningful human control. It distinguishes between institution-level delegated autonomy and action amplification, through which speed, scale, common dependencies, behavioural correlation and interconnectedness may extend the effects of machine action beyond the institution. The analysis shows that agentic finance does not displace established model and organisational governance but introduces a governance fit problem concerning how regulated institutions confer, constrain and remain accountable for consequential machine authority.

detail.abstract: Most evidence on the relationship between housing and fertility focuses on house prices and the cost of financing them. We take a step back and ask whether the growth of the housing stock, a tangible quantity on which policymakers can act directly, shapes fertility. A two-period quantity-quality model with a minimum housing requirement and a predetermined housing supply implies that equilibrium fertility rises with the housing stock per household. Guided by this mechanism, we estimate the effect of housing-stock growth on fertility using a panel of the 50 Spanish provinces over 2001-2022. System-GMM estimates indicate that a one-percentage-point increase in the annual growth rate of the housing stock raises the contemporaneous total fertility rate (TFR) by roughly 0.7 percent on impact. If the higher growth rate is sustained, the cumulative response reaches about 5.5 percent in the long run. The effect operates almost entirely through first-birth rates, consistent with housing availability lowering the barrier to entering parenthood, although period data cannot distinguish whether women have first births earlier or whether fewer remain childless. Both open-market and subsidized housing growth raise fertility, with effects of statistically similar magnitude per standard deviation of growth in our preferred System GMM estimates.

detail.abstract: In this article, we derive residual-to-state bounds and study memory-kernel identification for physics-informed conformable diffusion with positive causal memory. A neural network approximates the state. The conformable derivative is local. A separate history integral carries the memory. For state-error control, a running-maximum argument gives a stability constant independent of memory strength and kernel mass. A uniform positive local coercivity margin yields a sharp coefficient that remains bounded as the time horizon grows. These estimates assume existence, regularity and a one-sided reaction bound. They allow nonintegrable time-weighted kernel mass. A finitesample estimate connects the continuous bound to neural training. It separates comparison, optimization, quadrature and sampling errors. For memory-kernel identification, normalized beta mixtures represent the unknown kernel modulation. Constrained variable projection determines their weights. A polynomial excitation condition establishes identification from an exact state. Positive roughness regularization ensures a unique penalized fit. The implementation imposes initial and boundary data exactly. It uses Gauss-Jacobi quadrature and safeguarded training with fixed block weights. Six synthetic problems assess state approximation and kernel recovery. Across five paired noiseless runs, profiling reduces mean relative modulation error from 7.46% to 0.787%. In a separate three-seed study at 1% noise, a penalty selected using held-out state data reduces this error from 20.8% to 9.8%. The gain is smaller at 3% noise. Lagged weighting has no uniform advantage. BDF2 is faster and more accurate on the timed forward tests.

detail.abstract: This paper compares a process-based crop model (SIMPLE), statistical models, and machine learning models for U.S. Corn Belt yields over 2000-2019. The statistical model substantially outperforms the process-based model, with national out-of-sample R 2 of 0.844 versus 0.413, and captures extreme-heat damage that the process-based model misses-notably the 2012 drought, where forecast errors are 10.9% versus 35.7%. Under CMIP6 climate scenarios, the models diverge sharply: the statistical model projects corn yield declines of 32-44 bu/ac as extreme heat exposure more than doubles, while the SIMPLE-based regression projects changes of only +3 to roughly 0 bu/ac. XGBoost corroborates the statistical model's projected losses; LASSO with interaction terms extrapolates unreliably for soybeans under novel climate conditions, highlighting a prediction-versus-projection tradeoff in flexible ML models. An adaptation counterfactual suggests that earlier planting may offset about 30% of warming-induced losses, though this estimate is not statistically significant. These results, which generalize to soybeans, imply that reliance on process-based models alone may substantially understate climate risks to U.S. agriculture.

detail.abstract: Small businesses play an important role in India's economic development by creating employment, supporting local production, encouraging innovation, and generating income for millions of households. Despite their contribution, many small business entrepreneurs continue to experience financial difficulties arising from limited access to formal credit, inadequate financial management skills, unpredictable market conditions, and growing competition. The expansion of financial technology (FinTech), particularly mobile banking and digital payment services, offers new opportunities to address some of these challenges. However, the benefits of digital financial services depend partly on entrepreneurs' ability to understand financial information, evaluate financial products, manage digital transactions, and make informed business decisions. This article examines the relationship between financial literacy, mobile banking adoption, and entrepreneurial resilience in India's small business sector. Using a conceptual literature-based approach, the study explores how financial knowledge can influence the effective use of mobile banking and how digital financial services may support business continuity, liquidity management, access to finance, and recovery from economic disruptions. The discussion also considers barriers such as digital fraud, limited technological awareness, unstable internet connectivity, and unequal access to financial services. The article proposes an integrated conceptual framework in which financial literacy strengthens the effective adoption of mobile banking, while mobile banking supports entrepreneurs' capacity to respond to financial shocks. It argues that financial literacy and FinTech should be developed together rather than treated as independent solutions. The findings presented as conceptual arguments may inform policymakers, financial institutions, entrepreneurship development agencies, and researchers seeking to strengthen the resilience and sustainability of small businesses in India's evolving digital economy.

detail.abstract: Technical standards play a central role in modern innovation systems, particularly in communication technologies where interoperability requirements shape technological development. Empirical studies of the relationship between patents and standards have traditionally relied on patent declarations submitted to standard-setting organizations. While such declarations provide useful signals of potential relevance, they rarely provide claim-level evidence linking patented technologies to specific technical clauses within standards documents. In several technology domains, declaration data are also incomplete or absent, limiting their usefulness for empirical analysis.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author, Patricia Funk, declares that she has no relevant or material financial interests that relate to the research described in the paper: “Confidence of Job Market Candidates: Is there a Gender Gap?”
declarations.ethicsApproval: We had a survey as part of the project. The ethics committee of the Università della Svizzera italiana gave a positive decision on 17.12.2025 (Ethics Committee Decision CE-2025-43).

detail.abstract: This paper provides the first large-scale evidence of a gender gap in confidence among economics job market candidates. Our sample includes candidates from the top 100 economics departments who were on the market in one of the six seasons from 2019/20 to 2024/25. We measure confidence in their job market papers by combining a bag-of-words approach, which counts hedges (signals of lower confidence) and boosters (signals of higher confidence), with a large language model (GPT-5), which identifies expressions of uncertainty specifically related to the authors' own research. Both approaches reveal a robust gender gap: female candidates write in a less confident way than male candidates. As we control for department X cohort fixed effects, gender differences in research quality are expected to be small on average. We further document with a survey experiment that writing style matters for how research is evaluated: holding research content constant, a less confidently written paper leads to a lower assessment of research quality.

title: Collapse: Many Hands, No Hand on the Whole. Housing, Then the Economy: A Canadian Story and Lessons to Be Learned

detail.abstract:
Between 2020 and 2026 Canada's housing market went from boom to collapse. In the Greater Toronto Area, new home sales in 2025 were the lowest in 45 years, a record 7,243 condominium units were cancelled, about 3,000 pre-sold units were taken back from buyers who could not close, and housing starts fell to levels not seen since 1996, all during a national housing shortage. Was this bad policy, the market, or someone to blame?

This paper argues that it was none of these alone. Seven levers shaped the market: interest rates, immigration volumes, mortgage rules, taxes and charges on new homes, approvals, the pre-sale model of financing, and an economy that had come to lean on housing. Each was held by a different institution, and each was pulled, often for good reasons, within that institution's own mandate. But a home takes four to six years to build, while rates and immigration change in months, and the levers moved quickly, often and all at once. No one had the job of asking what they would do together, to whom, and when. The paper calls this many hands and no hand on the whole. It does not excuse the hands: looking around is part of the job, and the paper assigns each institution a graded share of responsibility.

Because Canada's economy leans on housing more than almost any other, the damage did not stay in housing. The paper follows it into the trades, suppliers, household debt, municipal budgets and the lives of young people, and separates it honestly from the trade war with the United States, which was a distinct shock. Five invented people, each labelled, carry the story from the inside.

Applying the four checks of Channels, Not Dams, the paper finds that every check stopped at the edge of a single mandate. It proposes an independent Impact Guidance Office to assess and publish the combined effect of major decisions before they are made, with a public dashboard, warnings that must be answered within 45 days, and a panel of those affected, alongside seven targeted repairs, including the resident-led and at-cost housing models proposed earlier in the series.

detail.abstract: I construct a new series of U.S. trade policy uncertainty (TPU) shocks from the events of the two episodes of the U.S. trade war, in 2018-2019 and 2025-2026, measured as the change in a daily newspaper-based TPU index around each event. Using these shocks, I study the transmission of U.S. TPU shocks to 29 advanced and emerging economies. Estimated over the whole trade war, the effect of TPU shocks on other currencies against the U.S. dollar is close to zero, but this estimate hides responses of opposite sign in its two episodes. TPU shocks depreciated other currencies in 2018-2019 and appreciated them in 2025-2026, and the responses of trade, prices and policy rates changed sign with them. Only in the second episode did they act as a negative demand shock for the rest of the world. In both episodes, the response of the exchange rate reflects the premium that investors require to hold other currencies instead of the dollar, which rose in 2018-2019 and fell in 2025-2026.

detail.abstract: Organizational goals determine the direction of management decisions, especially when an organization must choose among several equally plausible alternatives. This article discusses the relationship between organizational goals and managerial decisions through a case study of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GoTo) in 2022-2026. The discussion is conceptual and analytical, drawing on the views of Simon (1955, 1964), Cyert and March (1963), Mintzberg et al. (1976), and Locke and Latham (2002), while the case data come from business news and company disclosures. The discussion shows that GoTo's shift in goals from growth to profitability, namely a positive adjusted EBITDA without additional external funding, changed the criteria used to assess alternatives. Expansion through heavy promotions was no longer pursued, while cost efficiency and a strategic partnership with TikTok were carried out. The result can be seen in adjusted EBITDA, which moved from minus IDR 16.01 trillion in 2022 to roughly IDR 2 trillion in 2025. The planned merger with Grab remains an open decision because it touches other goals, namely national interest and the welfare of driver partners. In conclusion, clear and measurable goals serve as decision premises and criteria, so goals need to be formulated before alternatives are assessed.

detail.abstract: Shipment delays are among the most frequent and costly exceptions in manufacturing supply chains, yet many organizations still detect and resolve them through threshold-based alerts and manual planner triage. This paper presents the design and evaluation of a delay resolution agent: an agentic decision system that predicts international shipment delays, scores their operational severity, selects a response under a tiered-autonomy policy, and executes actions through integrations with a transportation management system (TMS) and a team messaging platform. The architecture combines a Random Forest delay classifier with a transparent rule-based severity layer and a decision policy engine, rather than relying on a large language model for operational decisions, to preserve auditability, latency, and cost predictability. Low-risk actions are executed automatically, medium-risk actions require planner approval, and high-impact disruptions are escalated for human-led resolution. The system is evaluated on a synthetic dataset of 48,000 international shipments modeled on an automotive parts inbound network, together with a discrete-event simulation of planner workflows. On a held-out six-month test period, the classifier identified 68.1% of delayed shipments in transit (precision 0.58, ROC-AUC 0.87), compared with 20.7% for a carrier-ETA rule. In the simulated base case, mean time to resolution for delayed shipments fell from 33.8 to 16.4 hours (−51%) and planner workload fell by 39%; across staffing and handling-time scenarios the reduction ranged from 31% to 93%. detail.abstract: This paper examines how online customer reviews, user-generated content (UGC) and influencers shape brand reputation on marketplaces, social media and other digital platforms. The aim is to describe the mechanisms through which these three sources affect consumer trust and to propose an approach to managing them as a single system. The study is conceptual. It draws on a narrative review of Russian and international literature on corporate reputation, electronic word of mouth (eWOM), social proof and influencer marketing, a synthesis of published empirical findings, and a document analysis of Russian, EU and US regulation and of marketplace rules. The analysis shows that each source generates a distinct type of trust: reviews produce collective trust, UGC produces experience-based trust, and influencers produce personal trust. Key risks are identified, including fake reviews, covert advertising and the transfer of reputational crises from an influencer to the brand. The paper proposes a "trust triangle" model in which the three sources form a closed cycle: influencers bring customers to the product page, reviews confirm or refute the influencer's promise, satisfied customers create UGC, and the most active creators become brand ambassadors. The model implies that a break in any link of the cycle is more damaging than the weakness of a single source. Four propositions for empirical testing and practical recommendations for reputation management are formulated.

detail.abstract: We uncover a novel stylized fact about the interest rate exposure of business development companies (BDCs): unlike traditional banks, BDCs exhibit substantial positive net interest income exposure to rising interest rates. BDCs predominantly hold floating-rate loans while financing their investments with a combination of fixed-and floating-rate debt. This balance sheet structure allows interest income to rise more than interest expense when rates increase. Yet, despite this favorable exposure, BDCs contract new lending following monetary tightening, accompanied by a decline in average spreads on newly originated loans and a shift toward safer borrowers. We argue that three distinctive features of BDC intermediation model help explain this disconnect: floatingrate lending increases borrowers' debt-service burdens and credit risk, market discipline makes BDCs' funding costs sensitive to portfolio risk, and payment-inkind (PIK) provisions create contingent liquidity demands on lenders precisely at a time when the shadow cost of liquidity is higher. Together, these features can transform positive interest rate income exposure into heightened credit and liquidity risks that constrain lending. Our findings highlight how interest rate risk transferred to borrowers can feed back to intermediaries, weakening credit supply even as their reported income increases.

detail.abstract: Zero-trust security has become an important approach to protecting cloud-native infrastructure by requiring workloads to satisfy explicit security and compliance policies before deployment. In Kubernetes environments, admission controllers and policy engines enforce these requirements by validating or modifying resource requests. However, additional security checks may increase admission latency, complicate deployment workflows, and introduce dependencies that affect cluster reliability. This article examines the relationship between zero-trust guardrails, admission performance, and operational resilience through a structured review of relevant literature and technical documentation. It considers policy complexity, webhook execution, request concurrency, failure handling, and architectural dependencies as key sources of potential overhead. The analysis suggests that security effectiveness should not be evaluated solely by the number of enforced policies. Instead, organizations should assess enforcement coverage alongside latency percentiles, timeout rates, deployment success, and policy-service availability. The article proposes a performance-aware admission framework that combines efficient policy evaluation, selective enforcement, and resilience-oriented configuration. It concludes that zerotrust guardrails can strengthen Kubernetes security without imposing disproportionate operational costs when security decisions are designed, measured, and maintained as part of the platform architecture.

detail.abstract: Discrete choice experiments (DCEs) are an important tool for understanding consumer preferences, and a central design choice is the number of alternatives shown in each task. Increasing the number of tasks is costly, whereas adding alternatives within a task is relatively inexpensive, yet guidance on choice-set size remains largely heuristic. We show that choice-set size affects the statistical and computational performance of a broad class of estimators through a single curvature constant of the log-likelihood. Increasing the choice set creates richer comparisons within each task but also reduces the probability that each alternative is chosen, leading to a non-monotone relationship between choice-set size and this curvature constant. We further provide a matching lower bound, demonstrating the tightness of this dependence, and show that the convergence of proximal gradient descent is governed by the same constant. Numerical experiments demonstrate that an appropriately chosen choice-set size can achieve the same predictive accuracy using up to 75% fewer tasks.

detail.abstract: This paper reviews existing research on the challenges of adopting artificial intelligence in human resource management, focusing on implications for workforce planning in supply chain organizations. While AI-enabled HR systems may improve forecasting, skills analysis, scheduling support, and administrative efficiency, adoption is constrained by data fragmentation, limited analytical capability, integration costs, unclear accountability, employee distrust, privacy concerns, and algorithmic bias. These challenges are especially consequential in supply chains, where workforce decisions interact with safety, time pressure, labour variability, and operational continuity. The review synthesizes literature on AI-HRM, HR analytics, human-AI decision-making, and supply chain risk management. It proposes a staged adoption framework built around readiness assessment, bounded piloting, governance, human oversight, and ongoing evaluation. The paper argues that successful adoption should be measured not only by efficiency but also by fairness, transparency, employee experience, and resilience.

detail.title: Rethinking the Supply Chain Risk Management Process: Insights from a Case Study with Remote Sensing Technology and Machine Learning Analytics

detail.abstract:
Purpose
Global supply chains are increasingly exposed to disruptions that evolve faster than traditional supply chain risk management (SCRM) processes can detect and respond to. Advances in machine learning (ML) enable new forms of data-driven risk analysis for SCRM. This study examines how the integration of remote sensing technologies, related data, and ML-based analytics is reshaping the established SCRM process. The study focuses on highlighting changes in established SCRM processes as well as the resulting implications for information processing in supply chains.

Design/methodology/approach
The study draws upon Information Processing Theory and Business Process Reengineering Theory in order to examine the shifts in the information processing capacity and the changes in the established SCRM process. The study employs a case study within the context of deforestation related supply chain risks and geographical artificial intelligence methods. These methods combine remote sensing data and ML-based analytics.

Findings
As a work-in-progress paper, empirical findings are currently under development. However, initial results indicate that that the combination of digital technologies enable a shift from reactive to proactive risk management.

Practical implications
The study is expected to provide practitioners with a more profound understanding of how digital remote sensing technologies reshape information processing capacities and present a novel process for SCRM.

Originality/value
The study intends to propose a novel SCRM process that arises from the integration of digital technologies, specifically remote sensing technologies, specifically remote sensing technologies which have the potential to transform the information processing capacities of firms.

detail.abstract: This thesis examines whether the timing of the Wasserstein ambiguity radius can be driven by observable information and have economic value distinct from its average level. We construct a misalignment signal from daily, weekly, and monthly return distributions, aggregated around a Wasserstein barycenter and compared using Sliced-Wasserstein distances. The signal modulates the radius of a W 2 ambiguity set in a linear-loss portfolio problem, evaluated through a point-intime walk-forward design over 1995-2025. In the main universe, the net Sharpe ratio increases from 0.6892 to 0.7451, a gain of 0.0559. Neither the paired HAC test nor the paired bootstrap establishes a general improvement at the 5% level. Signal-ordering placebos reject the interchangeability of the observed temporal ordering, and the main specification remains significant after max-T adjustment within both the four-cell and twelve-cell families. A modulation based on realized volatility nevertheless achieves a slightly higher point estimate, without a significant paired difference. The contribution is therefore primarily methodological: the level and timing of the ambiguity radius can be distinguished and tested, but the signal's incremental economic value has not been established.

detail.abstract: Many micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) struggle to survive even though their products are good. This article asks why this happens and to what extent managerial decision quality explains it, by analyzing one real case: the Pempek Chindo MSME in Karawang, reported by Taufik et al. (2025). The approach is a qualitative case study based on secondary data, framed by bounded rationality, cognitive bias, and dynamic capabilities. The analysis shows that the business survives through adaptive but shortterm and intuitive decisions. This pattern leaves vulnerabilities: dependence on platform promotions, financial records that are not yet structured, unused access to formal financing, and no medium-term planning. Among four alternatives assessed with a weighted matrix, diversifying sales channels together with simple financial record-keeping scored highest (4.00). Decision quality is the most controllable direct cause, but it works together with capital constraints and digital platform conditions, so it is not the only cause.

detail.abstract: Change is inevitable for organizations operating in a dynamic business environment. However, large-scale changes implemented all at once often trigger resistance, high risk, and operational disruption. This article aims to explain how the incremental model helps organizations cope with change gradually. The method used is a literature review with a descriptive case discussion of Toyota (kaizen) and Netflix (the transition from DVD rental to a streaming service). The findings show that the incremental model helps organizations through four mechanisms: reducing risk, facilitating organizational learning, reducing resistance, and maintaining operational continuity. Nevertheless, the model is inadequate when an organization faces a crisis that demands rapid and radical change. Therefore, incremental change needs to be combined with a clear strategic direction so that small steps do not lose their purpose (Quinn, 1978; Weick & Quinn, 1999).

detail.title: Effects of Extreme Temperature Exposure on Learning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest

detail.abstract: As temperatures rise, understanding how extreme heat impacts student performance becomes increasingly important. This paper examines how exposure to high temperatures affects student learning and exam performance through cumulative channels. Using administrative records from Cambodia’s grade 12 national examination (2014–2023) linked with high-resolution reanalysis climate data, we estimate the impact of sustained heat during the school year on learning, proxied by exam scores. Our findings reveal that sustained exposure to high temperatures significantly reduces test scores, particularly among students in the social science track. A 1°C increase in average school year temperature lowers social science scores by roughly 0.05 standard deviations, suggesting that heat hampers the accumulation of learning over time. The results underscore that heat affects human capital formation and that adaptation capacity varies across socioeconomic and demographic groups. Students in the science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) tracks and those accustomed to hotter climates display partial resilience, while female social science track students remain disproportionately exposed. Policy responses can improve classroom infrastructure and scheduling to reduce cumulative heat stress. Understanding these pathways is essential for designing education systems that remain equitable and resilient in a warming world.

detail.abstract:
In an increasingly globalized workplace, international managers play a vital role in leading teams composed of individuals from diverse cultural, linguistic, and professional backgrounds. This study examines the challenges faced by international managers in managing culturally diverse teams and the strategies adopted to foster effective collaboration, team cohesion, and organizational harmony.

The study adopted a qualitative research design. In-depth virtual interviews were conducted with 15 purposively selected international managers representing diverse industries, including financial services, telecommunications, agriculture, and marketing. The interview data were analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns, themes, sub-themes, and managerial responses to cross-cultural challenges.

The findings revealed three major categories of challenges: differences in work styles and ethics, communication barriers, and cultural orientations. Managers reported that variations in time management, language proficiency, and perceptions of authority often hindered team cohesion and operational efficiency. In response, managers adopted strategies including simplified communication methods, cross-cultural training workshops, participatory management approaches, and team-building activities designed to promote inclusivity and cultural awareness. These strategies were perceived to enhance team productivity, responsiveness, collaboration, and employee satisfaction.

The study is limited by its small purposive sample of 15 international managers and its reliance on qualitative self-reported data, which may limit the generalizability of the findings to other organizational and national contexts. Future studies could employ longitudinal and mixed-method approaches to examine the sustainability and broader applicability of cross-cultural management interventions. The findings provide practical guidance for organizations and international managers seeking to improve the effectiveness of culturally diverse teams. Organizations should strengthen cross-cultural training, adopt adaptive communication practices, encourage participatory leadership, and develop inclusive team-building mechanisms to manage cultural differences and improve team performance. The study highlights the importance of cultural awareness, inclusivity, mutual respect, and effective intercultural communication in promoting harmonious workplace relationships. Effective management of cultural diversity can contribute to reduced interpersonal conflict, greater employee inclusion, and more cohesive multicultural workplaces. The study contributes to the cross-cultural management literature by providing qualitative evidence on how international managers identify and respond to culturally diverse team challenges across multiple industries. Its value lies in linking specific cross-cultural challenges with practical managerial responses, thereby providing an integrated perspective on adaptive leadership and sustainable collaboration in multicultural work environments.

detail.abstract: Research in entrepreneurial finance examines external support through recipient-firm outcomes. Yet support directed at firms can also shape employees' careers, raising questions about whether the firm is the right boundary for understanding value creation and appropriation. detail.abstract: Frontier laboratories and the safety researchers who leave them describe advanced artificial intelligence in a shared eschatological register. The prophetic exit has consolidated as an institutional genre. Exit converts institutional office into prophetic authority, where risked equity certifies the sincerity of the warning while leaving its evidentiary basis unchanged. By 2026 the warning has become a corporate position, endorsed by the laboratories themselves amid sovereign co-investments and twenty-year commitments of nuclear power. An apocalyptic horizon survives disappointing product cycles, supplying the patience that multi-decade infrastructure investments require. Within the research field, symbolic capital favors describing misconfiguration exploits as machine volition, and evaluation designs that foreclose alternatives produce the behaviors their threat models predict. In litigation, published warnings establish the notice that defeats a superseding-cause defense. In regulation, the same vocabulary directs oversight toward speculative model capability and away from execution privileges, culminating in an executive accord that ratifies corporate self-governance. The warning that certifies the machine's power becomes the alibi that shields its custodians.

detail.abstract: We study the management of productive, depreciating real assets under a collateral constraint, proportional sale costs, and a fixed payout share. Motivated by real estate investment trusts, we construct and globally verify the policy that maximizes expected discounted distributions. Purchases occur at a unique endogenous threshold, while sales restore feasibility at the collateral limit. Higher sale costs or price volatility widen the optimal precautionary buffer, although greater volatility strictly reduces optimal distribution value. The value function provides a benchmark for comparing purchase rules with constant thresholds from a common initial balance sheet. We derive an exact value-loss decomposition that distinguishes the costs of premature purchases from those of delayed expansion. Requiring more financing slack before purchasing delays or leaves unchanged the first forced-sale intervention under the same price shocks, but strictly reduces distribution value beyond the optimal threshold. Numerical illustrations show how inherited borrowing can limit this protection and how its magnitude varies with the evaluation horizon.

detail.abstract: Before deciding whether to intervene in an AI-assisted process, someone has to recognise a reason for closer review. This paper asks how an available signal becomes such a reason when its meaning is uncertain. I distinguish noticing an observation, understanding what it may imply, identifying a question that needs checking and choosing a justified next step. A reason to review is not proof of danger, and neither determines the operating response on its own. The proposed contribution is a question-centred synthesis of these judgments, extended by a rule for keeping a material unanswered question linked to evidence and accepted follow-up. The individual elements have established predecessors. Hypothetical water-monitoring cases illustrate how context, independent observations and earlier closure reasons can change whether further assessment is justified. Two proposed studies test those information conditions. A separate comparison, P1, tests the follow-up rule after questions have already been identified; it does not test recognition. No study has been conducted, and the cases require specialist review. Any benefit must be weighed against missed concerns, unnecessary checking, delay and burden.

detail.abstract: Leadership in Nigeria has long been a subject of intense debate because persistent challenges undermine national development, political stability, and social cohesion. This essay examines the nature and roots of the leadership conundrum in Nigeria through a historical lens, exploring the legacy of colonialism, post-independence governance struggles, military interventions, and systemic socio-political challenges such as corruption, nepotism, and lack of visionary leadership. Drawing on a literature review, the discussion contextualises these leadership deficits within broader themes of moral decay, weak institutions, and ethnic factionalism. The essay further explores the link between leadership and national security, highlighting how leadership failures exacerbate insecurity and underdevelopment. Finally, it proposes a way forward grounded in moral reorientation , institutional reforms, democratic consolidation, and inclusive governance, offering lessons for Nigeria's leadership to harness its rich human and natural resources effectively for sustainable development.

detail.abstract: Recent work on "gradual disempowerment" argues that incremental AI development could erode human control over civilization through competitive pressure, describing the displacement as unauthored drift. In institutional life, displacement occurs through attestation, the act by which a natural person signs, certifies, or adopts an output as an official act. "Human Parroting" is the practice of attesting to machine output that the signatory has not verified and could not explain. It preserves the form of human oversight while abandoning its substance in exchange for speed. The law has met this practice repeatedly. Courts sanction lawyers who file fabricated citations. Regulators refuse algorithmic opacity as an excuse for adverse credit decisions. Tribunals bind enterprises to chatbot statements, and European law treats nominal human review as no review. Custom does not set the standard of care, and competitive pressure does not convert delegation into necessity. The language of drift removes from the record the party that law holds responsible. That party is the missing defendant.

detail.abstract:
Total Portfolio Approach (TPA) is usually discussed in a single-asset-owner setting: one institution, one governance structure, and one definition of success. That setting is powerful but incomplete. Many asset managers serve several clients through one investment platform, and they all face versions of the same question: how to preserve TPA benefits when the word “total” no longer refers to a single client.

We develop the Tailored Total Portfolio Approach (TTPA), an extension of TPA to multi-client settings. We map the design space for multi-client TPA, define its vocabulary, and distinguish between the investment platform as the unit of production and the client portfolio as the unit of fit.

TTPA is like made-to-measure tailoring: a common base is cut once and adjusted where client needs genuinely differ. Clients define objectives, the asset manager defines what the platform can produce in common, and the boundary between them is a joint determination. TTPA aims to preserve the benefits of scale while improving client fit.

detail.abstract: Recessions shift the pool of unemployed toward the more skilled. We show that the participation margin demonstrates the same skill gradient, i.e., in downturns the nonemployed with higher predicted wages hold on to the labor force proportionally more than those with lower predicted wages. Overall, the participation margin contributes to roughly a quarter and a third of the unemployment volatility of the highskilled and low-skilled workers, respectively. A representative-household RBC model with search-and-matching frictions, heterogeneous worker types, and a participation choice can account for these differential cyclical sensitivities. Two forces drive the skill gradient in the participation margin: low-skilled workers are more discouraged by falling job prospects, and job loss raises attachment more among high-skilled workers.

detail.abstract: Around the globe, Small, Medium and Micro Enterprises (SMMEs) represent the foundational engine of economic development, socioeconomic stability, and employment creation. This is also true in emerging economies such as South Africa. Despite their socioeconomic significance, SMMEs have notoriously high failure rates, with up to 70% of these entities failing within their first five years of operation. While various reasons for the latter dispensation have been researched, scholarly consensus links it directly to the absence, inadequacy, and/or ineffectiveness of internal control systems. While enterprise-level internal control frameworks serve as global gold standards, their structural assumptions clash fundamentally with the operating realities of SMMEs. This scoping review presents a rigorous comparative evaluation of conventional internal control frameworks against a newly updated, practitioner-orientated framework. Using a dialectical lens of thesis and antithesis , this study ascertains structural voids, operational feasibility, and inherent limitations, as guided by applicable methodological frameworks, and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. The synthesis demonstrates why enterprise-level internal control frameworks cannot be transplanted "as-is" into SMMEs due to financial and operational requirements that are beyond the reach of SMMEs. In turn, the practitioner-orientated framework organic pathway is very favourable for SMME adoption, but it has critical theoretical and structural vulnerabilities. The study provides a conceptual synthesis and diagnostic matrix that justifies the necessity of scaled SMME control architectures while offering concrete recommendations to fortify the practitioner-orientated framework against its inherent limitations.

detail.abstract: We quantify the impact of Robinhood traders on the US equity market. Within a structural model of asset demand, we estimate investor-specific demand curves for retail and institutional investors and derive aggregate pricing implications from market clearing. Robinhood traders exhibit substantially different demand curves from all other investors, including households. Their demand is the most elastic, their portfolios tilt most strongly toward volatile and micro-cap stocks, and their latent demand responds sharply to large absolute recent returns, reflecting attention-driven trading. While their aggregate impact is small on a value-weighted basis, per dollar of invested wealth, Robinhood traders exert the largest price impact of any investor group, including hedge funds. Their high marginal impact raises concerns about the surge in Robinhood assets and mobile-first retail brokerages more broadly: during the 2020 lockdown, Robinhood trades explained over 13\% of the variation in small-cap returns.

detail.abstract: We study an online resource allocation problem in which each arriving request is earmarked for a single resource but can be made flexible at a loss of utilization. The decision maker must choose upon arrival whether to honor the earmark or allow assignment to any resource. We compare two regimes: deferred flexible assignment, in which flexible requests are assigned after the entire arrival sequence is observed, and immediate flexible assignment, in which these assignments must be made upon arrival. Against a common clairvoyant fluid benchmark, we establish nearly tight competitive guarantees in the small-demand regime. For deferred assignment, a policy that draws a single flexibility-ratio threshold before the horizon achieves a competitive ratio of 0.794, nearly matching an upper bound of approximately 0.7942 for any online policy. For immediate assignment, we introduce tracking policies that coordinate allocation decisions with the evolution of the fluid benchmark for observed demand. A factor-revealing potential argument and computational certification yield a competitive ratio of 0.717, while an upper bound of approximately 0.7267 limits the performance attainable by any online policy. Together, these results show that postponing flexible assignments until all demand is observed improves the best achievable worst-case guarantee by about seven percentage points. Thus, carefully designed immediate-assignment policies recover most of the performance attainable with deferral, despite committing resources before future demand is revealed.

detail.abstract: This paper quantifies how investors’ portfolio demand responds to price changes at long horizons versus short horizons. Using investor trades — changes in portfolios — at different horizons, I first present reduced-form evidence that elasticities increase significantly over time. detail.abstract:
Background:  The crude cesarean delivery rate (C-CDR) is widely adopted to evaluate obstetric care quality, yet it fails to account for inter-hospital heterogeneity in patient baseline risk. We aimed to evaluate whether the risk-adjusted primary cesarean delivery rate (RA-PCDR) serves as a more robust indicator for obstetric quality assessment, by benchmarking against an official hospital obstetric quality rating system.

Method: This retrospective study utilized 391,661 electronic medical records (EMRs) from 56 tertiary hospitals in a Chinese province (2017–2019). Using 290,184 EMRs from women without prior cesarean delivery, we constructed and cross-validated a risk-adjusted primary cesarean delivery rate (RA-PCDR) model using a mixed-effects logistic model, adjusting for 12 prespecified maternal and fetal covariates. The RA-PCDR and crude cesarean delivery rate (C-CDR) were calculated annually for each hospital. Their longitudinal concordance with the official Key Clinical Specialty (KCS) obstetric quality tiers was then assessed to compare their alignment with this independent benchmark.

Findings: Among 391,661 deliveries from 56 tertiary hospitals, the RA-PCDR demonstrated consistent positive associations with KCS quality classifications across all study years, whereas the C-CDR showed weak and nonsignificant associations. For the 4-tier KCS classification, Kendall τ values for the RA-PCDR ranged from 0.203 to 0.293 across individual years and reached 0.498 over the 3-year study period (all P < .05), compared with values ranging from −0.007 to 0.128 for the C-CDR (all P > .05). Similar findings were observed using the 6-tier KCS classification, with a 3-year Kendall τ of 0.552 for the RA-PCDR (P < .001) and 0.056 for the C-CDR (P = .57).

Interpretation: In this study, the RA-PCDR demonstrated substantially stronger agreement with independently established hospital quality classifications than the C-CDR. These findings suggest that risk-adjusted cesarean delivery metrics may provide a more valid measure of obstetric care quality and support their incorporation into hospital quality assessment frameworks.Funding This work was funded by the General Program of the National Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No. 72474011), affiliated with the Department of Management Sciences (Discipline Code: G0406, Health Management and Policy).

detail.abstract: Employee engagement and retention are shaped by interacting leadership practices, cultural norms, and the systems through which organizations make decisions about work. This conceptual review examines how inclusive leadership, organizational culture, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled human resource management may be integrated to support employee voice, psychological safety, perceived organizational support, and longer-term attachment to work. Drawing on foundational theories and recent reviews of inclusive leadership and AI-assisted human resource management, the paper synthesizes established findings while distinguishing them from propositions requiring empirical validation. Inclusive leadership can signal that employees are valued and able to contribute; an inclusive culture can embed those signals in everyday routines; and carefully governed AI tools can help identify workforce needs, personalize learning, and support timely interventions. These benefits are not automatic. Algorithmic bias, opaque recommendations, intrusive monitoring, poor data quality, and weak employee participation may undermine trust and reproduce workplace inequalities. The paper therefore proposes an integrated framework in which leadership and culture shape the conditions for responsible AI use, psychological and relational mechanisms connect organizational practices to engagement, and engagement contributes alongside job quality and labor-market conditions to retention outcomes. The framework emphasizes human oversight, transparency, data minimization, participatory design, and continuous evaluation. It offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to use AI without displacing the relational responsibilities of managers, and outlines a research agenda centered on longitudinal, multilevel, and cross-context studies. The paper is conceptual and does not report original experiments or claim causal effects beyond the evidence reviewed.
